histoire: Élève de deuxième année au lycée préfectoral de jujutsu de Tokyo. Camarade de classe de Satoru Gojo et de Shoko Ieiri. Il utilise la « Technique de manipulation de fléau », qui lui permet d'absorber les fléaux qui se rendent et de les contrôler à volonté. Il accorde de l'importance à la courtoisie et croit qu'il faut sauver les non-exorcistes.

analyse: A Blue Hybrid debuffer whose damage mostly arrives outside her own turns, through two independent follow-up systems — Pursuit from S2 and Follow-up from S3. Open with both and re-apply on expiry; S3's Crit RES Down overwrites rather than stacks, so recasting it early buys only the refreshed timer.

Both auto-attacks are a coin flip, and crits fix that: her own crit makes Pursuit guaranteed, an ally's crit makes Follow-up guaranteed. Her S1 self-buff and S3's Crit RES Down are therefore consistency tools, not just team utility — and Crit Rate memories do double duty.

Follow-up only fires off “影â€ (Blue) allies using Command or Ultimate skills, so she is hard-gated to mono-Blue and wants allies who attack; buffers and healers give her nothing, and Cooperative Ultimates are excluded.
Her most underrated line is the debuff amplification on Follow-up, boosting the enemy's most recent debuff by a tenth of its value — she is better beside other debuffers than her own numbers suggest.

She is durable for a debuffer, with innate evasion and Stealth at the start and again below 40% HP, and that defence feeds her offence: Stealth Count only climbs on turns she avoids skill damage, so staying untouched is what scales her ULT.

Her weakness is multi-target content — Pursuit chases her marked enemy and Follow-up hits one random target out of an AoE, scattering her debuffs. Both follow-up debuffs also cannot be buffed, so amplification supports only improve her S2 and ULT. Best pointed at a single priority target in a Blue squad that already has a carry worth amplifying.

analyse: A pure Red-team amplifier — every debuff he applies is “幻â€ (Red) Type exclusive, so he gives literally nothing to a mixed squad. His raw debuff totals are lower than the top-tier supports, so he is picked for consistency and uptime rather than for peak numbers.

His best argument is that the passive aura is not a conventional debuff: it ignores the debuff-reduction modifiers that hard content leans on, so it holds its value in exactly the floors where most debuffers quietly stop working. That alone can justify the slot over a stronger-on-paper support.

The whole character is a ramp, and the numbers that matter are 6 (aura on) and 15 (50% cap); the 20 his ULT wants is a milestone most fights never reach. Open with S2 to cross the threshold as early as possible — the aura is the payoff and every turn below 6 is wasted.

Stack growth is less reliable than it looks: outside S2 casts he only gains counts when the enemy actually debuffs him, so against clean-hitting bosses he can stall well short of the cap. Plan on S2 carrying the ramp and treat the passive gains as a bonus, not a schedule.

His aura and his cast debuffs are separate effects, not one stack — S3 lands on top of the passive rather than being wasted. That is why you keep casting S3 after the cap, and why his real ceiling is higher than either effect looks alone. Hold the ULT until the aura is capped; fired early it throws away most of its scaling.

Judge him as a support, not a damage dealer — no Black Flash, and his damage is incidental even with a scaled ULT. Build him to survive: the aura is deleted the moment he dies or leaves the field, which is the worst thing that can happen to a team built around him.
histoire: Vieil homme d'âge indéterminé, directeur du lycée préfectoral de jujutsu de Kyoto. C'est aussi le principal chef de file des conservateurs dans le monde actuel des exorcistes. Il veut éliminer Itadori, qui a absorbé Sukuna.

analyse: A pure Green support who deals essentially no damage of his own — his entire job is stacking Information Gathering and converting it into a steady stream of buffs for a mono-Green team.

Information Gathering is the engine behind everything. He builds stacks passively each turn (more if he avoids taking a hit) and through S3, and almost every effect he casts — his S1 damage buff, S2's defensive layer, his ULT and his passive — scales up with how many stacks he has banked, so keeping him alive and untouched is what powers his ceiling.
His ULT is his highest-impact tool: it fills a large amount of Ultimate Gauge for the rest of the Green team and layers on Jujutsu and Green Damage Dealt buffs on top.

S1 costs nothing and feeds the team a scaling Green Damage Dealt buff, making it a free filler he can throw out every turn to keep the amplification topped up. S2 layers on a flat Jujutsu buff plus a stacking damage-reduction, and once his passive stacks are high it also charges the team's Ultimate gauge.

S3 is his utility button: it stealths him (protecting his stacks from being knocked off), banks extra Information Gathering and disrupts the enemy — a low-cost way to stay safe while the engine keeps spinning. His passive quietly turns his stacks into persistent team buffs and, if he ever leaves the field, hands the survivors a parting buff and Ultimate gauge.

The catch is that he is completely mono-Green — outside a full Green line-up he does nothing, and he brings no personal damage, so he only earns his slot on teams that can convert his buffs and gauge dumps into real output. In the right Green core, though, he is a top-tier enabler.

histoire: Élève de première année au lycée préfectoral de jujutsu de Tokyo. Une exorciste venue de la campagne, dotée d'un fort esprit de compétition. Détestant de tout cœur sa ville natale fermée et exclusive, elle s'est inscrite au lycée de jujutsu malgré le danger, tout cela pour pouvoir aller en ville.
analyse: A blue attacker built around heavy, sustained area damage rather than a single burst window. Her S3 hits hard every time it comes up, and because her energy economy keeps it fueled, she can keep the pressure on turn after turn while her ULT serves as the payoff spike on top of it.

Her closest comparison is Yuta. He may edge her out on single-target damage, but Nobara brings something he doesn't: real area damage — and a big part of that is S3 (Straw Doll Technique "Resonance"), one of the highest AoE hits in the game outside of ultimates. If you need a blue carry that can clear a full wave rather than just delete one target, she's the pick over Yuta.

Nail Count is her central mechanic. S1, S3 and her ULT all apply it (more stacks against fewer enemies), and the ULT hits far harder against targets carrying Nail Count, scaling up the more stacks are on them before consuming the whole pile. The plan is simple: pile on Nail Count across the fight, then cash it in with the ULT.

Tropical Juice is her secondary resource and her damage switch. S2 (Praise of the Eternal Summer) spends a stack to give herself a massive DMG Dealt buff at no energy cost — and on top of that it actually refunds 20 Cursed Energy. Combined with the 20 she recovers at the start of battle, she rarely runs dry, which is what lets her keep firing her expensive AoE instead of having to ration it.

Her evasion loop ties the kit together and makes her a self-sufficient carry: her passive gives her a chance to evade each turn, and a successful evade grants crit rate and refunds Tropical Juice, so the longer she survives the more juice she generates to keep feeding S2. She also scales her own Jujutsu off the total number of debuffs on the enemy board, so debuff-heavy teammates push her personal damage even higher.

Rotation: spread Nail Count with S3 and S1 over the early turns while letting evades stockpile Tropical Juice, spend S2 on the turn before you ULT to load the DMG Dealt buff, then fire the ULT into a board full of Nail Count for the payoff. Rebuild Nail Count afterward, since the ULT wipes the stacks.

histoire: Élève de première année au lycée préfectoral de jujutsu de Tokyo. Inscrit comme exorciste de grade 2. Un génie, et le seul élève de première année autorisé à effectuer des missions en solo. Vivre, c'est protéger et sauver les personnes qui lui sont les plus chères.

analyse: A green debuffer built around stacking "夜" (Green) Damage Received on enemies, so his ceiling shows up specifically inside green-focused teams rather than as a universal support.

S2 (The Well's Unknown Abyss) is the core of his kit. Unlike older green debuffers, it lands BOTH Taijutsu and Jujutsu Green DMG Received at once on the target, and because that debuff chains with his ULT and gets refreshed by S1, the same stat-down can be pushed all the way up to roughly 150% on a target. That single-skill double debuff plus chaining is what defines him.

He effectively replaces Geto as the green stat-debuff anchor. Geto falls behind precisely because he only debuffs Taijutsu OR Jujutsu rather than both, and he doesn't carry that debuff into his ultimate the way this Megumi does — so where Geto caps out, Megumi keeps stacking.

S3 (Max Elephant) is the support layer: AoE Crit RES Down and Green Damage Received Up on every enemy, while handing the ally directly behind him in formation a crit rate, Taijutsu and Jujutsu package. Position your green DPS right behind him so that buff lands on the right unit.

ULT (Shikigami Combo) is his payoff turn — a hard-hitting AoE that layers another wave of Green Taijutsu/Jujutsu DMG taken, Break DMG taken and Crit RES Down on the whole wave, continuing the debuff chain started by S2 while refunding his own energy efficiency for the following turns.

S1 is utility, not a damage button — its job is extending the duration of the green DMG-taken debuffs already on the target, keeping the stacked stat-down alive without re-applying everything. The 3-turn cooldown means you weave it in, not spam it.

His value lives entirely in the debuffs — his own damage falls behind. He could have been stronger, but right now there's no real alternative for the role, so he's worth running regardless. Just be aware that a future green debuffer with more damage attached wouldn't have a hard time powercreeping him.

Rotation: refresh S3 every 4 turns to keep your DPS buffed (its crit/Taijutsu/Jujutsu buffs last exactly 4 turns), and spend the turns in between on S2 to keep the stat debuffs flowing onto the target. Fire ULT during the burst window to extend the chain, and fall back on S1 when you're running short on Cursed Energy — it costs nothing and still keeps the debuff timers alive.

analyse: A dedicated Yellow support whose entire kit pours stat and damage buffs into the rest of the team, both while he is on the field and after he leaves it. He brings almost no personal damage and is built purely to make a Yellow carry hit harder.

His S3 is the bread-and-butter buff: it stacks cleanly, comes with a small self-heal, and is cheap enough on energy that you can keep recasting it turn after turn without ever running dry. S2 feeds Cursed Energy to the team while charging his own Ultimate.

His Ultimate buffs the team and, more importantly, extends his own time on the field — and because he keeps CE flowing to allies, his presence alone keeps the whole rotation going while his gauge fills back up.

He runs on a timer through Urgent Business and will leave the battle once it expires, but his exit is a feature, not a drawback: on the way out he grants the team a permanent damage buff that cannot be removed or nerfed by enemies.

Dupes sharpen him further — at 1 dupe he hands the team extra Cursed Energy and gains Ultimate gauge for himself, and at 3 dupes he layers an additional passive damage buff onto allies for the whole fight.
Standard rotation is to open with S2, then S1, then spam S3 until the Ultimate is ready — a clean, low-maintenance support line.
histoire: Un enseignant capricieux et têtu du lycée préfectoral de jujutsu de Tokyo. Il adore jouer des tours aux autres et est reconnu par tous les exorcistes comme le plus puissant du monde. Il s'efforce maintenant de former la prochaine génération en alliés puissants afin que le monde des exorcistes ait un avenir plus radieux.

analyse: A Blue Taijutsu attacker built around Zone State, which he enters after landing a Black Flash. Once in Zone his skills unlock their extra effects and he snowballs hard, making him a reliable single-target damage dealer.
His Ultimate is the centerpiece — a heavy multi-hit nuke whose final blow is a guaranteed Black Flash that bypasses counters, so it lands cleanly even against defensive enemies.
S3 gives him solid break damage, and while he is in Zone it also stacks a Blue Damage Received debuff onto the target, softening the enemy for the rest of the squad.

S2 raises his own Black Flash rate and, while in Zone, pushes Ultimate charge to himself and the ally in front of him; opening with S1 beforehand makes those Black Flashes easier to land and helps him get into Zone in the first place.
The Taijutsu buff he pulls from Zone is special — it ignores enemy stat-reduction effects, so it holds up in high-difficulty content where ordinary buffs get stripped away.

His SP version is a major upgrade: more damage, Ultimate charge, Cursed Energy regen and a crit buff. The catch is that it is locked behind dupes (A1 and A3) — at A0 he works fine but his Black Flash output is noticeably less consistent for an attacker.
histoire: Élève de première année au lycée préfectoral de jujutsu de Tokyo. Un prodige qui n'apparaît qu'une fois par millénaire, capable de résister au poison virulent du roi des fléaux, Ryomen Sukuna. Il considère cette particularité comme une mission et se consacre personnellement à la lutte contre les fléaux.

analyse: An AoE Jujutsu attacker built around his Cursed Spirit Manipulation Technique, who floods the enemy team with debuffs and turns those debuffs into his own power. Note he cannot be fielded alongside Suguru Geto.

He stacks a wide spread of debuffs: a Red Jujutsu Damage Taken increase, an enemy damage-output reduction, Crit Resistance down, and a chance to Stop enemy actions — so the whole team benefits from playing through him.
S3 is his debuff anchor: it deals heavy AoE, lowers enemy damage, extends the duration of his signature Jujutsu Damage Taken stacks, and piles on extra Break Damage against Formidable Foes.

His Ultimate is a hard-hitting AoE that layers even more of his Jujutsu Damage Taken stacks on top of the existing ones, alongside stat and Crit Resistance debuffs — his single biggest debuff-and-damage moment.
The amount of debuff S1 applies scales with his Cursed Energy, and since S1 is his normal attack it costs no energy — so he can keep stacking debuffs for free while saving CE for his bigger skills.

He carries a deep passive suite — CE and Ultimate gauge generation, HP regen, melee damage reduction, evasion, and Poison/Rot immunity — and the self-buffs he gains from all those debuffs hold up even in high-difficulty content.

analyse: A Yellow Taijutsu attacker whose whole game plan is stacking Chain Counts to trigger Full Throttle Mode — a powered-up state that transforms his skills and unleashes his real damage potential.

His Ultimate is the switch: once he has banked enough Chain Counts it launches a big hit, refunds a large chunk of Cursed Energy, and drops him into Full Throttle, where his damage, crit and survivability all spike.
S3 is his fastest way to build Chain Counts, and in Full Throttle it transforms into a stronger multi-hit that also buffs his crit — so it carries him in both phases of the fight.
S2 sets up his defensive game: it taunts the target and puts him in a Counter State, then in Full Throttle it converts into a heavy strike with an extra Taijutsu buff.

His passive suite ties everything to Chain Mark — follow-up counter attacks, an AoE ignition that debuffs the enemy team and charges his Ultimate, plus evasion and crit buffs that scale as his Chain Counts climb.

The catch is fragility around his core mechanic: taking melee hits, being countered, or eating Blind can wipe his Chain Counts, so he is vulnerable to counter, evasion-denial and Darkness. Protecting his stacks until Full Throttle is the key to playing him well.

analyse: A Yellow Hybrid attacker whose skills all deal mixed Taijutsu & Jujutsu damage, wrapped in a self-sufficient package of sustain, buffs and debuffs. He is versatile enough to handle both single targets and waves.

His Ultimate is his hardest hit and ignores Darkness entirely, so blind can't shut him down. It also lands a Yellow Damage Received debuff and refunds a large chunk of Cursed Energy, keeping his rotation going.

S3 is his setup and execute tool: it stacks Break Damage Received and Yellow Damage Received debuffs on the target while dealing heavy multi-turn break damage, softening enemies for himself and the team.
S2 is his AoE clear, but it cleverly scales up the fewer enemies are present — so it doubles as strong single-target damage when only a boss is left standing.

He starts the fight with a large Cursed Energy pool and keeps topping it up: S1 (his normal attack) feeds him crit and energy, his crit passive grants more, and his Ultimate hands back a big lump on cast.

His Reversal Cursed Technique passive keeps himself and the lowest-HP ally healed, and the more he crits the larger his own Taijutsu & Jujutsu buff grows — so he snowballs damage while sustaining the team, making him a low-maintenance Yellow carry.

analyse: A Blue support and stat buffer who builds his kit around summoning a Cursed Corpse, using it to fuel high damage buffs for the team and to shield his allies. He is the glue of a Blue squad rather than a damage dealer.
S3 is his core team buff: a stacking Taijutsu & Jujutsu boost handed to the whole Blue team, and it is what the rest of his kit is designed to keep running.
S2 buffs the team's crit rate, summons the Cursed Corpse, and extends the duration of his Blue stat buff — so it ties his summon and his buffs together in a single cast.

His Ultimate is a debuff bomb: it applies Disruption, a chance to inflict Darkness, and a Blue Damage Received increase while lowering the enemy's Crit Resistance and damage output, softening the target on every front.

The summoned Cursed Corpse tanks melee hits for himself and his allies, deals a follow-up attack and applies a debuff once per turn — but its HP scales off his own, so building his HP keeps the Corpse alive and his shielding online.
Practical tip: lean on S1 and any Cursed Energy support to keep his energy topped up, since his value comes from casting his buffs consistently rather than from raw damage.

analyse: A Green Hybrid attacker whose whole kit revolves around Cursed Energy, backed by an unusually deep set of passives. He blends personal damage with team support, getting stronger the more CE he has banked.
His ULT is his hardest hit — big mixed damage with a high crit chance and solid break damage, while also dropping a Crit Resistance and Green Damage Received debuff on the target to set up the team.

The CE threshold is the key mechanic: at 60 or more Cursed Energy his S2, S3 and ULT all hand the Green team a damage buff, and his S3 and ULT scale their own damage up with CE — so managing his energy is what unlocks his ceiling.

He sustains his own CE through landing Black Flashes and through a passive that dumps a large chunk of energy, a stat boost and ULT gauge on a later turn, helping him keep firing his expensive skills.
His passive suite is what makes him so durable and flexible: crit and Black Flash buffs, a counter, and a revive that pulls enemy aggro onto him and cuts the damage he takes afterwards.
He also ramps his ULT and Black Flash rate based on how many Tokyo Jujutsu High Officials and Year 1 allies are on the team, so he rewards themed Green line-ups.
Rotation note: S3 can't land a Black Flash but hits hard, so use S2 to fish for Black Flashes and fire S3 for raw damage — all while keeping an eye on his Cursed Energy.
histoire: Un exorciste de grade 1 qui a démissionné de son poste d'employé de bureau. Un cadet de Gojo au lycée. Il avait compris que la carrière d'exorciste, c'était de la merde alors qu'il était encore lycéen, puis a découvert qu'être un employé ordinaire, c'était pareil après avoir travaillé dans une entreprise normale. Finalement, il a décidé de devenir exorciste, ce en quoi il excelle, et un adulte très mûr.

analyse: A versatile Red support and stat enhancer who buffs the team and debuffs enemies on essentially every action. Almost everything she casts contributes something, so she is hard to misplay and slots into most Red line-ups.
S2 is her control and buff tool: AoE damage that stuns and blinds the enemy team while handing the Red squad a big Taijutsu & Jujutsu buff that stacks with her Ultimate's version.
S3 is her debuff tool — it stacks a Red Damage Received and Break Damage Received debuff on all enemies, so the rest of the team hits much harder into the targets she softens.
She layers evasion through S3, her Ultimate and a passive, and every successful dodge feeds her Cursed Energy back, keeping her skills running and making her surprisingly slippery for a support.

Her standout mechanic is Enemy Scan: her skills and Ultimate build stacks that her Intelligence Sharing passive converts into a steady, scaling buff for the whole Red team. Critically, that buff resists the buff-stripping found in high-difficulty content.
Because all of her skills and her Ultimate produce a buff or debuff, she performs well even left on auto — there is no wrong button to press, making her a low-effort engine for a Red team.

analyse: A Yellow Jujutsu debuffer built around the Freeze Enhancement mechanic and damage-over-time. She is a slow burn who thrives in long fights, where her sustained debuffs and stacking Freeze DoT pile up into serious damage.

Freeze Enhancement is her engine: as its level climbs it buffs her Jujutsu, weakens enemies, hands her Cursed Energy, and upgrades her skills into stronger versions that apply even more DoT and debuffs — and at higher levels it even carries a true Stun chance.
S2 applies a Yellow Jujutsu Damage Received debuff, and S3 adds Freeze DoT plus a Break Damage Received debuff; once upgraded, both skills hit harder and spread their debuffs to the whole enemy team.

Her Ultimate is a respectable multi-hit AoE that blankets enemies in Freeze DoT and, against targets already loaded with Freeze, detonates for bonus damage while pushing her Freeze Enhancement level even higher.
She stays alive on her own through a Reverse Cursed Technique passive that heals her whenever her HP dips low, giving her the longevity she needs to reach the drawn-out fights she is best in.

The debuffs she generates through Freeze Enhancement resist the debuff-stripping found in high-difficulty content. Practical tip: cast S3 early to immediately bank a few levels of Freeze Enhancement and get the snowball rolling.

analyse: A Green Taijutsu enhancer who deals respectable damage himself while showering the Green team with crit, Black Flash and damage-dealt buffs plus enemy debuffs. He is a damage amplifier first and a sub-attacker second.

S3 deals damage and stacks a Damage Dealt buff onto the Green team. S2 is similar but adds extra crit and Black Flash rate for himself — the trade-off being that it runs on a cooldown rather than being spammable.
His Ultimate is a multi-hit finisher that pairs a Green Damage Received debuff on the target with another team-wide Damage Dealt buff, so it amplifies the squad even as it nukes.

Landing a Black Flash flips him into Zone State, where he gains a stacking self-buff tied to his Black Flash count and hands the Green team Black Flash rate and Ultimate gauge — turning him into a team-wide engine.

Zone also upgrades his skills: S1 gains a no-cost Green Damage Received debuff, S2 adds a Break Damage Received debuff, and S3 layers on a Crit Damage buff — so being in Zone is where his full kit comes online.

He carries a Counter that can trigger every turn and protects the whole team, buffing allies on a successful counter (and Zone raises its activation rate). On top of that, every crit or Black Flash he lands feeds the Green team more Damage Dealt and crit rate, making him a buff machine for Black-Flash-heavy Green comps.

Il considère cette particularité comme une mission et se consacre personnellement à la lutte contre les fléaux.

analyse: An effectively invincible Blue Taijutsu attacker who doubles as a support, layering buffs and debuffs onto the fight while he builds toward his Domain. He stays untargetable until it fires, so he rarely needs protecting.
His ULT is the payoff — a true Stun that even disables enemy Ultimate counters, applies a Damage Received debuff, and lands one of the biggest AoE hits in the Blue pool all at once.
S2 is his main rotational skill: AoE damage that stacks a Crit Resistance debuff on enemies while buffing his own Taijutsu, so it gets stronger the more you cast it.
S1 is a multi-hit that racks up break damage with a high Black Flash chance; when he lands a Black Flash his passive rewards him with a damage buff and some healing, keeping him self-sufficient.
S3 deals Jujutsu damage and applies a Break Damage Received debuff, and his passive piles extra damage onto enemies already in Break State — so he pairs naturally with break-focused teammates.

He is forced to cast his ULT after ten turns and leaves the field afterwards, but on the way out he buffs the surviving allies. Crucially his ULT always charges and deals damage even under stage restrictions, so he stays reliable in difficult content. Cycle S2 and S1 while you build up, then close with the Domain.
histoire: Un enseignant capricieux et têtu du lycée préfectoral de jujutsu de Tokyo. Il adore jouer des tours aux autres et est reconnu par tous les exorcistes comme le plus puissant du monde. Il s'efforce maintenant de former la prochaine génération en alliés puissants afin que le monde des exorcistes ait un avenir plus radieux.

analyse: A Red Hybrid debuffer who deals heavy mixed damage while consistently stacking Crit Resistance down and Red Damage Received debuffs — softening enemies for the team as he fights. He transforms mid-battle to ramp up.

S3 deals high break damage and layers on multiple debuffs; once his Ultimate gauge is high enough it transforms into a powerful Taijutsu Black Flash attack, which is also key to unlocking his Ultimate.
His Ultimate applies even bigger debuffs and damage, heals him, and puts him into Spirit Body State — a transformation that buffs his stats and upgrades all of his skills into stronger Soul versions.
S2 is his AoE: it damages all enemies and applies a Red Damage Received debuff, and in Spirit Body State its upgraded form also charges his Ultimate gauge faster, accelerating his loop.
Landing a Black Flash puts him into Zone, where his passive grants self stat buffs, HP and Cursed Energy recovery, and faster Ultimate charge — keeping him self-sufficient.

Important: he cannot cast his Ultimate until he has performed a Black Flash at least once in the battle (his transformed S3 is the cleanest way to do this). The self-buffs from Spirit Body State also resist the buff-stripping found in high-difficulty content.
histoire: Un fléau né des êtres humains. Il peut modifier l'apparence des humains en touchant leur âme. En tant que fléau tout juste né, il est fasciné par son pouvoir et répète sans cesse des expériences sur les humains avec innocence.

analyse: A Yellow Jujutsu attacker who pairs huge damage multipliers on his skills and Ultimate with stacking Laceration damage-over-time, all wrapped in heavy self-sustain. He can carry a fight largely on his own. Note he cannot be fielded alongside Yuji Itadori.
His Ultimate is his finisher: a guaranteed-crit single-target nuke that also leaves behind a Flame DoT, doing colossal damage in one button.

S2 is his AoE: it applies Laceration DoT and a Damage Received debuff, and when only one enemy remains it transforms into an even stronger single-target hit — so it stays useful from wave clear all the way to bosses.
S3 is a hard-hitting multi-hit that also stacks Laceration; its raw damage is exceptionally high even by attacker standards, making it a key part of his burst.

He is extremely durable: a passive grants immunity to most status effects (Poison, Darkness, Stun, Confusion and more), a Counter that punishes melee attackers, and reliable HP regen through Reverse Cursed Technique.

His passives also keep him fueled and scaling — his damage rises with his current Cursed Energy, and he regains energy and buffs after landing crits or successful counters. Two caveats: his Ultimate cannot be used in a Combo Ultimate, and he must use both S2 and S3 at least once in the battle before the Ultimate unlocks.
histoire: Le roi des fléaux, qui a vécu il y a plus de mille ans et continue de menacer le monde présent même après sa mort. À l'apogée du jujutsu, les exorcistes ont rassemblé toutes leurs forces pour le défier, mais ont été vaincus. Il s'est incarné dans le corps d'Itadori, qui a absorbé son doigt, et proclame haut et fort son intention de massacrer toute l'humanité.

analyse: A Green Taijutsu attacker who doubles as a support, built around his Best Friend mechanic — he pours huge buffs into a chosen ally while dealing consistent damage himself. He wants a strong partner to amplify.

His Ultimate flips him into Highest Peak☆JUMPING! status: a guaranteed multi-hit nuke that also grants him a Taijutsu buff, raises his follow-up chance, and upgrades his other skills into stronger versions for the duration.

S3 is his main multi-hit damage skill, and once in Highest Peak☆JUMPING! it hits harder and grants extra crit rate. He also feeds himself stat buffs whenever he lands a crit or Black Flash through a passive.
S2 buffs his own Taijutsu and crit rate and, crucially, tags the ally in front of him as his Best Friend — and a Counter passive then protects and buffs that Best Friend whenever they are attacked.

After every turn he has a chance at a follow-up attack that buffs both himself and his Best Friend, and if two Black Flashes land in the same turn he unleashes a special attack that grants damage and Black Flash rate to both of them.

He also carries a Simple Domain passive that reduces the damage he takes while an enemy Domain is active, giving him a measure of safety. Overall he is at his best in a Black-Flash-focused Green team paired with a carry he can designate as Best Friend.
histoire: Élève de troisième année au lycée préfectoral de jujutsu de Kyoto. Bien que considéré comme une figure clé de l'école de Kyoto, il a des passions singulières et c'est un exorciste de grade 1 encombrant. Il est un fan passionné de la grande idole Takada.

analyse: An adaptable Red Taijutsu attacker who can switch between two stances — Nimble Style and Ferocious Style — each giving his skills a different set of effects, letting you flip between defense and all-out offense as the fight demands.

His Ultimate is a guaranteed-hit Black Flash whose damage scales with how much Cursed Energy he has spent beforehand (not stored) — the more energy you burn through his skills first, the harder it hits, becoming one of the biggest single hits in the game when fully fed.
S3 deals damage and buffs his own Taijutsu; in Nimble Style it also charges his Ultimate, while in Ferocious Style it transforms into a much higher-damage strike — making it good in both stances.
S2 in Ferocious Style becomes a multi-hit break attack with a guaranteed crit, giving him heavy burst and break pressure when he commits to offense.

In Nimble Style, S1 and S2 give him taunt, damage reduction and evasion, and a passive rewards every successful dodge with a Taijutsu buff and Cursed Energy — so the defensive stance also fuels his energy for the Ultimate.

His kit is loaded with crit, Black Flash and self-buffs, and landing a Black Flash triggers Zone for even more stat gains. After his Ultimate he enters Guaranteed Exorcism, which lets him stack Cursed Energy faster and freely swap styles each turn — so each subsequent Ultimate is easier to push to max damage.
histoire: Élève de première année au lycée préfectoral de jujutsu de Tokyo. Un prodige qui n'apparaît qu'une fois par millénaire, capable de résister au poison virulent du roi des fléaux, Ryomen Sukuna. Il considère cette particularité comme une mission et se consacre personnellement à la lutte contre les fléaux.

analyse: A single-target Blue Hybrid attacker who comes into his own in Rika State, where his skills convert to Jujutsu damage and he pumps out consistent high damage. Getting into that state is the whole point of his rotation.

His Ultimate is the key that turns him on: it deals heavy single-target Jujutsu damage, restores a big chunk of Cursed Energy, and grants Rika State — a long-lasting transformation that buffs his Jujutsu and keeps refunding energy each turn.

S3 applies a stackable damage-amplifying debuff to the target and buffs himself, and in Rika State it becomes an even stronger Jujutsu hit that also boosts his Crit Damage — making it his main damage button.

S2 buffs his stats and charges his Ultimate; in Rika State it transforms into a much stronger, longer-lasting buff (and adds a Crit Resistance debuff on enemies), though that version cannot be stacked.

His passives give him a crit buff and a Counter every turn, and landing crits or successful counters reward him with healing, Cursed Energy and Ultimate gauge — keeping him self-sufficient and ramping toward Rika State.

The standard line is to fire the Ultimate as soon as possible to enter Rika State, use S2 once to lock in its strong buff, then spam S3 for the bulk of his damage. His Rika State buffs also resist the buff-stripping found in high-difficulty content.
histoire: Un lycéen de dernière année qui voulait autrefois mourir à cause de Rika, sa petite amie transformée en fléau. Depuis son inscription au lycée de jujutsu, sa vie est devenue plus positive grâce à la camaraderie qu'il y a trouvée. Il a décidé de lever la malédiction de Rika.
étiquettes: Malus : dégâts de BREAK reçus accrus

analyse: A New Shadow Style, crit-based Yellow Defender whose job is to keep himself and the team alive while buffing the Yellow squad's damage. He protects through counters and damage interception rather than raw bulk.

His team damage buff comes from landing crits: a passive that grows stronger with every Critical Hit performed over the course of the battle, scaling up to a large team-wide Damage Dealt boost — so the longer he fights, the more the team hits.

S2 puts him into Simple Domain and a Counter State, cutting the damage he takes and letting him punish melee attackers; successful counters in turn feed him more crit rate, looping back into his buff engine.
His Ultimate is a guaranteed-crit AoE that also raises his own crit rate afterward, both dealing damage and fuelling the crit-stacking that powers his team buff.
S3 is a straightforward multi-hit that gives him plenty of chances to land the crits his kit revolves around.

Defensively he spends Cursed Energy and HP to intercept ranged damage and can outright prevent himself or an ally from being knocked out — a genuine team safety net. The catch is his passives drain CE heavily, so he leans on a Cursed Energy regen memory and S1 to stay funded.
histoire: Un exorciste de grade 1 qui enseigne au lycée préfectoral de jujutsu de Tokyo.

analyse: A crit-focused Red Jujutsu attacker built around Ember Insects and Flame damage-over-time, with the standout ability to act twice in a turn. He layers DoTs and burst damage while snowballing off his own crits.
His Ultimate is his big payoff: enormous AoE damage plus several stacks of Flame DoT at once, and a chance to halt the enemy team — easily his single hardest-hitting button.
S3 lowers the enemy team's damage while raising his own, and applies Flame DoT; S2 also lays down Flame DoT alongside its damage, so between the two he keeps the burn stacks ticking constantly.
Ember Insects are his engine: they buff his Jujutsu and upgrade S1 and S2 with extra hits and a Jujutsu Damage Received debuff, and they can be consumed to charge his Ultimate faster.
Landing three or more crits in a turn triggers his passive to grant a double-action state next turn, letting him effectively take two actions and chain even more damage and DoTs.

He is self-sufficient on resources — passive HP regen, Cursed Energy regen, crit buffs and automatic Ember Insect summons. To get the most out of him, build a team that supports crit and Cursed Energy so his double-action turns come up as often as possible.

analyse: A Red Jujutsu debuffer who leans on his shikigami both to survive and to stack damage-received debuffs that let the whole Red team hit much harder. He is a setup piece more than a damage dealer.
S2 deals damage while applying a stackable Taijutsu & Jujutsu Damage Received debuff to the target — his main tool for softening enemies turn after turn.

His Ultimate is his biggest debuff: a heavy Jujutsu Damage Received and Taijutsu & Jujutsu Damage Received stack on top of solid damage. The trade-off is that it removes both of his shikigami when cast.

S3 summons the Rabbit, which grants him attack immunity and soaks half the damage he takes while applying a Disruption and Damage Received debuff to the enemy team — his core survival and debuff button in one.
His passive auto-summons Divine Dog: Totality whenever his Cursed Energy is high enough, and having it out adds extra Jujutsu damage to his skills and Ultimate.

The optimal play is to keep both Divine Dog and Rabbit active at the same time, which unlocks the strongest versions of his skills and maximizes the debuffs from S2 and ULT. Since the Ultimate wipes both shikigami, try to bank enough Cursed Energy beforehand so you can resummon them right after.
histoire: Élève de première année au lycée préfectoral de jujutsu de Tokyo. Inscrit comme exorciste de grade 2. Un génie, et le seul élève de première année autorisé à effectuer des missions en solo. Vivre, c'est protéger et sauver les personnes qui lui sont les plus chères.

analyse: A break-specialized Blue Hybrid attacker who chips away with multiple attacks per turn through follow-ups and counters. His whole kit is wired around breaking enemies and punishing them while they are in Break State.
His Ultimate is his break finisher: very high break damage plus bonus damage against enemies already in Break State, and it also lowers the target's Ultimate count to delay their big move.
S3 (Projection Sorcery) puts him in a Counter State and inflicts heavy Confusion on the enemy, much like a smaller version of his Ultimate — a strong setup and disruption tool.

S2 grants him Projection Sorcery stacks (which power up his break effects) and a follow-up state, and refunds Ultimate gauge when used against an enemy in Break State — making it the engine that fuels his rotation.
His passives reward his playstyle: successful counters and follow-up attacks grant extra self buffs, debuff the enemy, and even buff the wider Blue team's stats.

Two real weaknesses to plan around: he has no taunt to force enemies into his counters, so he is poor against AoE and ranged attacks (his counter doesn't trigger on those), and his raw damage is low when he is not built up in his Projection Sorcery state.

analyse: A Yellow Taijutsu attacker who uses no Cursed Energy at all — every skill is free to cast. Instead his power comes from Combo Count, a resource that builds as the fight goes on and steadily ramps up his Taijutsu, so he gets stronger the longer he fights. He also layers Sting damage-over-time.

His Ultimate is his big single-target hit and stacks several layers of Sting, a bleed DoT that multiplies in damage with each stack — making it hit hard immediately and keep dealing damage over the following turns.

S2 first buffs his own Damage and Crit Damage and enters Sharpened Fang; while in that state it transforms into Pierce, which deals damage with bonus break damage and applies Sting — so it is both a self-buff and a damage tool.
He builds Combo Count from his skills, his Ultimate, and especially from breaking or defeating enemies, and a passive converts that count into a large scaling Taijutsu buff.
That same passive makes him quite durable: evasion chance, HP regen each turn, damage reduction, and immunity to some targeting effects — so he survives well without any healing support.

Most of his damage hinges on stacking Combo Count high, which can be slow to max in single-target or restrictive content. Practical tip: against mob waves use S1 to rack up combo quickly (it builds count per enemy hit), and rely on S2 to build and buff when facing a single target.

analyse: A Green Jujutsu attacker and debuffer who revolves around his Red Scale State — a self-buff stance that upgrades his skills, stacks poison and Damage Received debuffs, and lets him pump out heavy sustained damage.
There are two stages to the mechanic, and only the second one (Flowing Red Scale: Stack) unlocks his improved skills, so the core of playing him is reaching and keeping that second stage active.
S2 deals damage, applies a debuff, and is what enters or renews his Red Scale State; the state itself grants him a damage buff, a chance at heavy damage reduction, and ongoing Cursed Energy regen.
S3 applies poison and a Damage Received debuff, and once upgraded it deals extra damage, stacks more poison, and adds a Confusion-style Disruption to the target.
His Ultimate enters the Red Scale stack state while landing high poison and a Damage Received debuff; in the upgraded stack state it fires an additional hit for nearly double the output.

His Red Scale State and a passive both regenerate Cursed Energy, which is important because his improved skills cost more — the energy sustain is what lets him keep the upgraded stance running. Those self-buffs also resist the buff-stripping found in high-difficulty content, so prioritize keeping the second Red Scale stage up at all times.

analyse: A Yellow Jujutsu attacker who is built entirely around his Domain Expansion. Outside the Domain his damage is weak, but once it is up his skills transform into stronger 'Death Swarm' versions and he leans on a stacking, type-neutral DoT for his real damage.

His Ultimate expands the Domain, which is the centerpiece of his kit: it deals AoE damage, buffs his own Jujutsu, cuts the damage he takes, and blankets all enemies in a heavy Skandha DoT that amplifies as it stacks.
S3 raises enemy Damage Received and can delay/stop their actions; inside the Domain it becomes his main damage tool, piling on more stacks of the multiplying DoT.
S2 buffs his Jujutsu, reduces his damage taken, and speeds up his Ultimate charge — important since his Ultimate gauge is slow to fill — and inside the Domain it also deals AoE damage.

His big weaknesses are that he does little as an attacker before the Domain is active and his Ultimate gauge takes a long time to build; a passive can fully charge it once per battle to help him get the Domain online.

Inside the Domain his S3 drains a lot of Cursed Energy, so to keep his DoT damage flowing rely on his Domain S1 (which refunds energy), his passive, CE regen memories and ally batteries. The DoT itself is type-neutral, so it stays effective regardless of enemy element.

analyse: A Red Hybrid support whose main job is amplifying the Red team's damage — almost every skill he casts hands all allies a large Damage Dealt buff, while he himself contributes solid crit-based mixed damage on the side.

S3 is his biggest team buff and a strong single-target hit in one: it lands a guaranteed Critical Hit, applies a Break Damage Received debuff, and gives the whole Red team a hefty Damage Dealt boost. It runs on a cooldown, so it anchors his rotation.
S2 is his stackable filler buff — multi-hit damage plus a team-wide Damage Dealt increase that stacks with his other buffs — best used between S3 casts to keep the buff uptime high.
His Ultimate combines a heavy multi-hit finisher with a Red Damage Received debuff on the target and yet another team Damage Dealt buff, so even his nuke doubles as support.

He is built to crit constantly — his normal attack and passives keep stacking crit rate and Crit Damage, which both fuels his own damage and triggers a passive that feeds him Cursed Energy and stats on every crit.

He ramps over the fight: a passive on a later turn grants a chunk of stats, Crit Damage and Cursed Energy, so he gets stronger the longer the battle lasts. His S3 and Ultimate guarantee crits, which makes him very consistent at triggering all his crit-based effects.

The one weakness to plan around is that he is fairly Cursed Energy hungry — even with the energy his crits refund, his skills cost enough that he benefits from being paired with a battery ally or a CE regen memory to keep his buffs flowing every turn. Best used as a buffer-sub-DPS that keeps a Red carry's damage permanently elevated.

analyse: A Green support who blends a strong team buff with healing and cleansing, making her a reliable two-in-one backbone for Green teams. She brings no real personal damage — her value is keeping the squad buffed and healthy.
S2 is her main buff: a large Taijutsu & Jujutsu Stat boost to the whole Green team, plus Stealth on herself so she can buff and then duck out of danger.

S3 is her healing and cleanse tool: it restores an ally's HP, adds a heal-over-time, sharply lowers the value of their debuffs, and even shortens Poison damage — all for a very low Cursed Energy cost, so she can use it freely.

Her Ultimate does both jobs at once — it re-applies the Green team Taijutsu & Jujutsu buff and heals/cleanses the whole team, and it always acts before attack skills so the buffs and heals land before your carries move.
A passive self-heals her, grants Stealth and cuts her damage taken when she drops low, helping her survive without needing the team to protect her.

Like most healers her damage scales off a low base stat, so don't expect offense from her. Slot her into a Green team that wants both sustain and a stat buffer in a single unit, ideally one with enough Cursed Energy support to keep her acting every turn.

analyse: A Green Jujutsu attacker with a build-up, transformation-based kit. Early on he stacks Core of Cursed Energy and charges toward Honored One Mode; once transformed, his whole kit upgrades and his damage spikes dramatically.

Core of Cursed Energy is his scaling engine: each stack massively increases his Jujutsu Stat (up to a huge bonus at max stacks), and his skills, counter and revival all build stacks — so the longer he survives and fights, the harder he hits.

S3 is his transformation button: first it buffs his Ultimate charge and grants Attack Immunity, then once his gauge is high enough it converts him into Honored One Mode, and while transformed it changes again into a self damage buff plus a Counter.

His Ultimate, Hollow Purple, is a massive single-target nuke that is only usable in Honored One Mode — it is his payoff and hits harder the more Honored One turns remain when you fire it, rewarding casting it early in the transformation.

S2 is his cheap, spammable damage skill that also builds Core stacks (and in Honored One it gains near-guaranteed crits), while his S1 stacks a damage-reduction debuff on enemies to help keep the team safe and then converts from single-target into AoE once he is in Honored One — so he has answers for both single targets and waves.

He is remarkably durable for an attacker: near-permanent Attack Immunity early, a self-revival that refunds Core stacks, evasion at low HP in Honored One, and a counter that adds damage and stacks. The trade-off is that he needs setup time to stack Core and reach Honored One before he comes fully online, so he ramps rather than bursting from turn one.

analyse: A Blue Jujutsu attacker whose entire identity is acting twice per turn. His S3 puts him in Spirit Turtle State, and a passive grants him an additional action while it is active — so his core gameplay is taking two attacks every turn instead of one, on top of an evasion chance.

The catch is that Spirit Turtle has a built-in downside: while active it cuts his own Damage Dealt and slows his Ultimate charge. The trick is to re-cast S3 while already in the state, which flips that penalty into a damage buff and cheaper Cursed Energy costs — so the state goes from a drawback to a major power spike.

Inside Spirit Turtle his other skills upgrade: his S1 transforms into a strong multi-hit Taijutsu attack that costs no Cursed Energy, and his other attacks gain stackable damage buffs. Most of his real output comes from chaining these improved, often free skills across his two actions each turn.
S2 is his main nuke — a single-target Jujutsu hit with a self Jujutsu buff baked in — and his Ultimate is a bigger version of the same, so he stays a reliable single-target damage dealer.

He is fairly self-sufficient on resources: a passive recovers Cursed Energy when he is hit and another gives a one-time energy and Jujutsu boost, helping him fund his rotation. A practical caveat is that he needs a turn to set up Spirit Turtle and re-cast it before he is at full power, so he ramps rather than bursting immediately.

analyse: A straightforward, high-damage Red Taijutsu attacker. Unlike many modern units she has no complex gimmick or transformation — she simply buffs herself and hits very hard, which makes her easy to pilot and reliable.
S2 is her core setup: a large self Damage Dealt buff plus a Damage Received debuff on the target, so she casts it first to amplify everything she does for the next few turns.
S3 is her AoE clear — a hard-hitting two-hit strike to all enemies — making her strong against waves once her S2 buff is up.

Her Ultimate is her single-target nuke, and although she is a Taijutsu unit its damage is overwhelmingly Jujutsu-based, ignoring Darkness on its big hit so blind can't stop her payoff. Because of this, she benefits more from a memory that boosts overall Damage Dealt or Jujutsu than from a pure Taijutsu memory.

She has high Crit Damage baked into her normal attack and a passive that, once her HP dips, refunds Cursed Energy and grants a large stat boost — giving her a comeback spike in longer or tougher fights.

Her main limitation is that all her amplification is self-only — she brings almost nothing to the team beyond a small enemy debuff — so she works best as a pure damage slot in a Red squad that supplies her with buffs and Cursed Energy.

analyse: A Blue Taijutsu attacker who uses no Cursed Energy at all — every skill is free to cast. Her damage comes purely from raw Taijutsu, which she stacks up through her own buffs rather than relying on a battery.

Her defining mechanic is skill chaining: each skill applies its own State (Throwing Kunai, Slash Down, One Mighty Slash), and casting a different skill while one of those States is active unlocks bonus effects. Sequencing her skills correctly is the key to maximizing her output.

For example, her S1 grants crit while in Slash Down, her S2 buffs Taijutsu while in Throwing Kunai and adds Crit Damage in others, and her S3 fills Ultimate gauge or grants Crit Damage depending on the active State — so the order you press them in genuinely changes the payoff.
Her Ultimate is a heavy multi-hit Taijutsu nuke with a guaranteed critical on the final hit, and it refunds Ultimate gauge on use, helping her cycle back to it faster.

Thanks to her Heavenly Restriction passive she is also self-sufficient and durable: passive HP regen, damage reduction, an evasion chance, and a Taijutsu boost that scales higher the fewer enemies remain — making her especially strong against single bosses.

One important rule: she only gains her combo buffs by switching to a different skill each turn — repeating the same skill won't trigger them. So always rotate between her skills rather than spamming one, choosing the order based on what you need (for example leading with one skill for raw damage, another for crit rate).

Since she ignores Cursed Energy entirely, she slots cleanly into any Blue team without needing a battery, and frees that support slot for other buffers. Her main demand is simply playing her skill chain in the right order to keep her buffs rolling.
histoire: Élève de deuxième année au lycée préfectoral de jujutsu de Tokyo. Bien que née dans une famille d'exorcistes d'élite, elle n'a presque pas d'énergie occulte et ne peut même pas voir les fléaux sans lunettes. Dotée d'une condition physique exceptionnelle, elle vit en maniant des outils occultes.

analyse: A rare dedicated Healer who not only keeps the team alive but also greatly buffs the Yellow team's damage output, making her a strong two-in-one support for Yellow comps.
S3 is her offensive support tool: it applies a Damage Received debuff to an enemy while handing the Yellow team a large Taijutsu & Jujutsu Stat buff — the main reason she boosts team damage so much.
Her Ultimate further amplifies the whole team, raising everyone's Damage Dealt and Ultimate gauge charging rate, helping the squad cycle their big skills faster.
S2 is her main heal and cleanse: it restores an ally's HP and lowers the effectiveness of their debuffs, and it is cheap enough on Cursed Energy to use freely.
A passive backs her up with emergency team-wide healing whenever an ally drops to low HP, giving the team a safety net even on turns she acts elsewhere.

Important: all of her damage scales off Taijutsu, and her base stat there is very low, so do not expect meaningful personal damage from her. She also has tight Cursed Energy, so support her with a CE regen memory, an ally battery, or co-op Ultimates to keep her healing and buffing reliably.

analyse: A Red Jujutsu attacker who debuffs through his Cursed Speech mechanic: he stacks [Cursed Speech] counts on enemies, and his own attacks deal escalating bonus damage based on how many counts the target has. The whole kit is about building counts and then cashing them in.
S3 is his count-builder — an AoE that applies Cursed Speech to all enemies (extra counts against powerful foes) — so it is the skill you lead with to set up the rest of his damage.

His Ultimate is the payoff: a heavy AoE that deals massive bonus damage scaling with each Cursed Speech count (up to a huge multiplier at max), then consumes those counts. Stacking counts first and then firing the Ultimate is his core damage loop.

S2 is his control and team-support tool: a near-guaranteed Stun, a strong Taijutsu & Jujutsu Damage Received debuff on the target, and a big chunk of Ultimate gauge handed to his allies — so he doubles as a stunner and battery for the team.

The major catch is that almost everything he does sacrifices his own HP (more against powerful enemies), so he is constantly bleeding himself to deal damage. A passive self-heals him each turn, but he is fragile and pairs best with a healer or strong team sustain.

His Ultimate also boosts his Cursed Energy efficiency afterward, easing his energy demands. The standard rotation is to cast S3 a few times to pile up Cursed Speech counts (it applies even more against bosses), then unload the Ultimate for a massive count-fuelled hit — so he is a debuffer-nuker who rewards patient setup and good team sustain.
histoire: Élève de deuxième année au lycée préfectoral de jujutsu de Tokyo. Descendant des exorcistes de la Parole maudite, ses propres mots deviennent des armes de malédiction. Pour éviter de maudire quelqu'un par accident, il ne communique qu'avec des garnitures de boules de riz.

analyse: A Green Jujutsu attacker who deals ramping AoE damage through his Mechamaru Counts mechanic: he stacks counts on enemies, and his skills and Ultimate hit harder the more counts the target carries (up to double damage at max stacks). Note he cannot be fielded alongside Ultimate Mechamaru.
S2 is his low-cost count-builder and AoE — it applies Mechamaru Counts to all enemies and, with enough Cursed Energy, refreshes their duration so his stacks never expire mid-setup.
S3 is his main damage skill: it hits a single target plus the whole enemy team, applies more counts, and scales its damage with the counts already present — making it both a builder and a payoff.

His Ultimate is a big AoE nuke that scales hugely with Mechamaru Counts, consumes them, and also lowers all enemies' Ultimate counts to delay their big moves. Stacking counts first and then firing it is his core damage loop.

He synergizes heavily with Kyoto Jujutsu High allies — a passive ramps his Damage Dealt sharply based on how many are on the team — and he is immune to Darkness with strong built-in break damage, so he handles blind-heavy and break content well.

His limitations are twofold: reaching max Mechamaru Counts can be slow without Cursed Energy support (a CE regen memory or battery ally makes his ramp far smoother), and his Ultimate cannot be used inside most enemy Domains, which can interrupt his payoff in certain fights. Best built as an AoE carry in a Kyoto-themed Green team that supports his energy and lets his Mechamaru and affiliation buffs stack up.

analyse: A Green Taijutsu attacker built around her Batto Count: a stacking resource that her skills feed into and that a passive converts into scaling Taijutsu, Ultimate charge, Crit Damage and cheaper skills as it climbs. The whole kit is about building Batto stacks as fast as possible.

Her SP upgrades are what define her — without them she is a fairly underwhelming solo bruiser, but with SP unlocked she transforms into a top-tier Green pick. The huge jump comes from her SP passive and SP Ultimate, so judge her almost entirely on her SP form.

S2 puts her in a Counter State and Simple Domain — once her Batto Count is high enough it upgrades into an AoE that also builds more stacks, so it shifts from a setup tool early to a damage tool later.

S3 is her reliable single-target multi-hit that buffs her own crit and adds Batto stacks, and at high Batto Count it too upgrades to refresh her Counter and Simple Domain — making it strong throughout the fight.

Her Ultimate is a hard single-target hit that taunts the target into attacking her, then her Counter and Batto-building punish them for it; her SP Ultimate hits far harder and adds a big self crit buff.

One of her biggest strengths in her SP form is team support: every time she lands a Critical Hit she grants the whole Green team a large Taijutsu & Jujutsu Stat buff plus a crit rate boost — and since her kit is built to crit constantly, she keeps these team buffs running almost permanently, making her a Green-team enabler rather than a pure solo carry.

Simple Domain gives her Jujutsu damage reduction and nullifies enemy Domain effects, so she doubles as a safety valve against Domain Expansion content. She also scales up alongside other Kyoto Jujutsu High students through a passive that boosts her damage based on how many are on the team.
histoire: Élève de deuxième année au lycée préfectoral de jujutsu de Kyoto. Comparée à ses camarades à la personnalité marquée, c'est une fille naïve, honnête et ordinaire. Elle se bat pour échapper à la pauvreté, et elle suit la mode de près.

analyse: A Blue Jujutsu attacker who blends huge burst damage with stacking Laceration damage-over-time, scaling much of his kit off his current Cursed Energy. He is a single-target powerhouse built around his Domain Expansion. Note he cannot be fielded alongside Yuji Itadori.

S3 is his main nuke and the only skill that actually spends Cursed Energy; its power scales with energy in tiers, so at higher thresholds it deals dramatically more damage and applies more stacks of Laceration. His normal attack (S1) helps fund the loop by charging his Ultimate gauge on hit.

His Ultimate, Malevolent Shrine, is a massive AoE that ignores defenses (Sure-Hit, nullifies Attack Nullification), blankets enemies in heavy Laceration, refunds a large chunk of Cursed Energy, and raises his maximum energy cap — his single biggest damage moment.

The catch is that casting the Domain applies Skill Restriction to himself for a couple of turns, locking out some of his skills. During that window his S2 changes into a high-damage, energy-scaling strike that also reduces his own damage taken and debuffs the target, so you funnel into that skill while restricted.

S2 is also his free, reliable crit setup outside the Domain — it costs no energy and buffs his own crit rate and Crit Damage — making it a safe filler that feeds his King of Curses passive (which rewards crits with damage buffs and energy). His Laceration DoT, applied by his normal attack, S3 and Ultimate, stacks and multiplies over time, and it is both buffable and type-neutral, so it stays effective against any element.

He is extremely durable: a Reverse Cursed Technique passive heals him based on hits taken, and a passive grants immunity to most status effects (Poison, Darkness, Stun, Confusion and more). One team tip: if you run him alongside other Domain users, fire his Domain first, since casting another Domain afterward would cancel his.
Overall a self-sufficient Blue carry whose loop is to bank Cursed Energy, detonate the Domain, then keep the multiplying Laceration and energy-scaled hits rolling.
histoire: Le roi des fléaux, qui a vécu il y a plus de mille ans et continue de menacer le monde présent même après sa mort. À l'apogée du jujutsu, les exorcistes ont rassemblé toutes leurs forces pour le défier, mais ont été vaincus. Il s'est incarné dans le corps d'Itadori, qui a absorbé son doigt, et proclame haut et fort son intention de massacrer toute l'humanité.

analyse: A Blue Taijutsu Obstructor — a disruptor whose specialty is shutting down enemy buffs and defenses rather than pure damage. He strips buffs, taunts, and pierces Attack Nullification, making him a strong answer to bosses that rely on stacking buffs or going untargetable.

S3 is his core disruption tool: it nullifies Attack Nullification, taunts the target onto himself, weakens and shortens the enemy's buffs, and stacks a large Taijutsu Damage Received debuff — softening the target for the whole Blue team.

His Ultimate is a heavy Taijutsu nuke that also strips an even bigger chunk of enemy buffs, pierces Attack Nullification again, and piles on Damage Received debuffs — so it both removes the enemy's defenses and punishes them hard in one cast.
S2 is his self-buff: it raises his Taijutsu and crit while granting damage reduction that scales with his Cursed Energy, letting him tank as the taunt target while still hitting respectably.

Much of his kit scales with Cursed Energy (his damage and his damage reduction both improve at high energy), and a passive front-loads a big chunk of energy and stats at the start of battle so he comes online quickly.

His SP form turns him into a Blue-team enabler: landing crits then buffs the whole Blue team's Taijutsu (alongside self crit, evasion and damage reduction), and his SP normal attack adds its own Taijutsu Damage Received debuff. Best used as a debuffer-disruptor in a Blue squad, especially against buff-reliant or untargetable bosses.
histoire: Utilisateur de fléaux venu de l'étranger. Il combat avec une corde que les exorcistes de son pays ont mis des décennies à fabriquer. Il est plutôt puissant.

analyse: A Red Jujutsu attacker who doubles as a powerful team amplifier through his Domain Expansion, Infinite Void. He deals strong personal damage but his real value is the massive Damage Received debuff his Domain lands on the whole enemy team.

His Ultimate is the centerpiece: it applies a true Stun to all enemies for multiple turns, strips and locks their Ultimate counts, removes enemy buffs, and overwrites any enemy Domain while inflicting an enormous Damage Received debuff that scales with his Urgent Business count — set up over time it can more than double the damage the whole team deals to those enemies.

S2 is his AoE damage and debuff, hitting all enemies while lowering their Damage Dealt, and S3 is his high-multiplier single-target nuke with a self Jujutsu buff. Both cost only 1 Cursed Energy, so he can fire them freely every turn before committing his Domain.
His normal attack is a hard-hitting Black Flash skill, and landing a Black Flash triggers Zone State for bonus Jujutsu and crit — so he ramps his own damage simply by attacking.

Two important catches: casting his Domain applies Skill Restriction to himself for a few turns (locking out his other skills), and he is on a timer through Urgent Business — once it expires he leaves the field entirely. The longer he survives, though, the higher his Urgent Business count and the stronger his Domain debuff becomes.

He also starts with Attack Immunity, making him hard to kill before his Domain fires. Best used as a Red carry-amplifier: build up Urgent Business, drop Infinite Void to crater the enemy team's defenses, and let your other damage dealers capitalize.
histoire: Un enseignant capricieux et têtu du lycée préfectoral de jujutsu de Tokyo. Il adore jouer des tours aux autres et est reconnu par tous les exorcistes comme le plus puissant du monde. Il s'efforce maintenant de former la prochaine génération en alliés puissants afin que le monde des exorcistes ait un avenir plus radieux.

analyse: A Yellow Taijutsu attacker built around Zone State and Black Flash. He is a single-target bruiser whose damage spikes hugely once he enters Zone, where he gets to act twice per turn and his skills upgrade.

His Ultimate is the trigger: a guaranteed Black Flash nuke that also activates Zone State. While in Zone a passive grants him an extra action each turn plus big Taijutsu and Black Flash buffs and Cursed Energy — so the Ultimate effectively turns him into a double-acting powerhouse for a couple of turns.
The trade-off is that he cannot recast his Ultimate while Zone is active, so Zone is a burst window: enter it, unload two upgraded skills per turn, then rebuild toward the next Ultimate once it ends.

S2 builds his Ultimate charge normally, but in Zone it transforms — and its bonus depends on the order you use it: cast first for crit and Black Flash rate, or second for a flat Damage Dealt buff, rewarding clever sequencing across his two actions.

S3 is his break-damage hitter with self damage reduction, and in Zone it becomes an even harder-hitting version. Both skills get cheaper in Zone thanks to his passive's Cursed Energy efficiency, so he can chain them comfortably.

He has strong innate offense (high crit and Black Flash baked into his normal attack) and Poison/Soul resistance for survivability. A practical rotation is to cycle S2 and S1 outside Zone to charge his Ultimate, then once in Zone spam S3 for the heaviest hits across his two actions.

His one notable weakness is that he is fairly Cursed Energy hungry, so he benefits a lot from being paired with a battery ally or CE regen support to keep his skills flowing — especially during the Zone window where acting twice doubles his energy spend.
histoire: Élève de première année au lycée préfectoral de jujutsu de Tokyo. Un prodige qui n'apparaît qu'une fois par millénaire, capable de résister au poison virulent du roi des fléaux, Ryomen Sukuna. Il considère cette particularité comme une mission et se consacre personnellement à la lutte contre les fléaux.

analyse: Despite his Attacker label, this SSR Kaito plays as an all-in-one Yellow support: he batteries Cursed Energy, buffs the team's damage and Jujutsu, debuffs and stuns enemies, and provides damage reduction — a true utility hub rather than a damage dealer.
S2 is his support engine: it buffs the whole Yellow team's Damage Dealt and, with enough Cursed Energy, feeds them energy every turn — making him a battery as well as a buffer in a single skill.
S3 is his control tool: a near-guaranteed Stun plus an enemy Damage Dealt debuff and a strong team-wide damage reduction, letting him lock down a threat while protecting the squad.

His Ultimate is his biggest team buff — a large Jujutsu Stat boost to all allies (with an extra layer for Yellow allies) — and it improves his own Cursed Energy efficiency afterward, easing his upkeep.
A passive adds even more Cursed Energy support to the team over time, so between it and S2 he keeps energy-hungry carries firing their skills and Ultimates far more often.
His personal damage and stats are low, so don't expect offense from him. He is a pure enabler bundling energy, buffs, a stun and damage reduction into one unit.

Two limitations to plan around: nearly all of his buffs only apply to Yellow-type allies, so he is locked into mono-Yellow teams rather than mixed comps; and his Cursed Energy battery effects require him to keep his own energy above a threshold, so he needs careful energy management to keep feeding the team (unlike the simpler, unconditional R-rarity Kaito).
histoire: Élève de première année du campus annexe de Fukuoka du lycée préfectoral de jujutsu de Tokyo. Il accorde énormément d'importance aux règles, c'est pourquoi il éprouve de l'hostilité envers Itadori, dont l'existence enfreint la loi des exorcistes. Sa technique occulte est surtout adaptée au soutien, il manque donc d'expérience au combat en première ligne.

analyse: A Green Jujutsu debuffer-attacker built entirely around his White and Black Divine Dog shikigami. With both dogs summoned, all of his skills gain extra hits and upgraded effects, so keeping them on the field is the heart of his gameplay.

S2 is his setup button: it summons both Divine Dogs, deals damage, and applies a Green Jujutsu Damage Received debuff. The dogs also tank for him — they soak a portion of incoming damage and let his skills ignore Darkness, adding survivability on top of offense.

S3 builds his Ultimate charge and, once the dogs are out, transforms into a stronger hit that also lowers the enemy's damage and adds a follow-up — turning a simple charge skill into a real damage tool.

Even his normal attack (S1) gains big extra Jujutsu hits while the dogs are summoned, so he keeps strong damage going every turn, not just on his skills. A passive also boosts his damage heavily against enemies in Break State, making him excellent at capitalizing on broken targets.

His Ultimate scales heavily off having the dogs summoned, especially the Black Dog, which adds a big extra hit and a Damage Received debuff. Its Ultimate gauge fills relatively quickly, letting him cycle it often, and fully set up it is his largest single-target burst.

A passive gives the Divine Dogs a chance to launch follow-up attacks whenever any ally uses a Command or Ultimate skill, adding extra off-turn damage and more Jujutsu Damage Received debuffs — and his skills get cheaper to cast while the dogs are active.

His one demand is the setup turn to summon and maintain the dogs; without them his kit is much weaker. Best played as a Green debuffer-carry that opens with S2, keeps both dogs alive, and amplifies the whole Green team's damage through his stacking debuffs.

analyse: A Green Jujutsu attacker whose damage scales off how debuffed the enemy is. A passive boosts her own Taijutsu & Jujutsu based on the number of debuffs and statuses on the target — up to an enormous bonus — so she shines paired with debuffers who can pile effects onto the enemy.

Her Ultimate is her single-target nuke and deals Soul damage, letting it bypass certain defenses and threaten enemy souls directly — her biggest burst once the target is loaded with debuffs to feed her passive.
S2 chips a Jujutsu Damage Received debuff onto the target, and S3 buffs her own Damage Dealt while hitting hard — together they let her both set up and ramp her own offense between Ultimates.
Her normal attack also stacks a small, long-lasting Taijutsu Damage Received debuff, so even her basic hits contribute to softening the enemy over time.
She has innate Black Flash access, and landing one triggers a large Jujutsu buff and Cursed Energy refund through a passive — giving her a strong damage spike and helping fund her skills.

Her ceiling depends heavily on enemy debuff count, so she is mediocre on her own but excellent as a Green sub-DPS in a debuff-heavy team. The flip side is that she falls flat against debuff-immune enemies, where her scaling passive does nothing — but pair her with units that stack statuses on the target and she becomes a serious damage threat.
histoire: Élève de première année au lycée préfectoral de jujutsu de Tokyo. Une exorciste venue de la campagne, dotée d'un fort esprit de compétition. analyse: A Blue Jujutsu support-debuffer whose specialty is amplifying the team's damage against weakened enemies. A recurring theme in his kit is that his debuffs scale stronger the lower the target's HP, so he gets better as a fight wears the enemy down — making him a strong finisher-enabler.
S3 is his main debuff: it stacks a sizable Blue Damage Received debuff on the target that grows as the enemy's HP drops, softening it for the rest of the Blue team.
S2 cuts the enemy's Jujutsu Stat (also scaling with low enemy HP), reducing their Jujutsu damage output while charging his own Ultimate — a mix of offense-debuff and defensive utility.

His Ultimate is his payoff: an AoE that applies the Blue Damage Received debuff to all enemies and deals heavy Jujutsu damage, ideal once the enemy team is already low and his scaling is at its strongest.

The cost of his kit is his own HP — most of his skills sacrifice health to cast (more against powerful enemies) — but he offsets this with multiple self-heal effects on his skills and a passive, so he sustains himself through the bleed.

Unusually for a support, he also packs attacker-level damage — but it is concentrated almost entirely in his Ultimate, which lands a heavy AoE Jujutsu hit; his other skills are mostly debuff tools with minor damage. His main value remains as a Blue debuffer-amplifier, and he is best in a Blue team that capitalizes on his Damage Received debuffs, especially in drawn-out fights where his low-HP scaling makes his debuffs hit their ceiling.

analyse: A Red Taijutsu debuffer who fights with a gun, alternating between two ammo modes and amplifying the enemy team's Damage Received while chipping in follow-up attacks. She is a support-debuffer first, not a main damage dealer.

Her two reload skills define her: S2 loads Special Ammo (single-target with a low chance to delay the enemy) and S3 loads Enhanced Ammo (AoE that stacks a Damage Received debuff on all enemies). In practice you will almost always favor S3, since its stackable debuff is far more valuable than S2's unreliable delay — and while Enhanced Ammo is active, her follow-ups and S1 apply that debuff too.

Her standout mechanic is her Follow-Up Attack: a passive makes her fire bonus shots whenever an ally uses a Command or Ultimate skill, and her own skills and Ultimate ramp her Follow-Up rate up to 100%. Note that ally buffs and other follow-up attacks do NOT trigger it — only direct Command/Ultimate skills — so she pairs best with active damage dealers and debuffers rather than buff-bots.

Her Ultimate is her biggest debuff window: it applies a massive Damage Received increase to the target and maxes out her Follow-Up Attack rate for several activations — turning the whole team's actions into extra hits on a softened enemy.
She also brings light control (action delays) and a self-Conceal passive that hides her when low on HP, giving her some survivability despite being fragile.

Her personal damage is low, so her value is purely as a Red debuffer-amplifier: keep the right ammo loaded, fire her Ultimate to crater an enemy's defenses, and let her follow-up shots and Damage Received debuffs multiply the rest of the team's output.
histoire: Élève de deuxième année au lycée préfectoral de jujutsu de Kyoto. Membre de la célèbre famille Zen'in et sœur jumelle de Maki. Une provocatrice née.

analyse: A Green Taijutsu attacker who uses no Cursed Energy — every skill is free to cast, so she never needs a battery and slots cleanly into any Green team. Her damage is pure Taijutsu, built around crits and self-buffs.
Her Ultimate is her single-target nuke and its damage scales with her current HP — the healthier she is, the harder it hits — rewarding keeping her topped up rather than letting her take damage.
S3 is her crit setup: it grants a huge Critical Hit Rate boost and big break damage on a single hit, so you cast it to guarantee crits before unloading her bigger attacks.

S2 is her AoE and team debuff — it damages all enemies, applies a Taijutsu Damage Received debuff, and hits harder the fewer enemies remain, so it doubles as strong single-target damage against a lone boss.
Her crit-focused kit feeds itself: her normal attack stacks a Taijutsu Damage Received debuff on crit, and her high innate crit rate keeps that rolling, softening the target for the whole Green team.

Thanks to her Heavenly Restriction passive she is self-sufficient and durable — passive HP regen, damage reduction, and a Taijutsu boost that scales higher against fewer enemies — making her especially strong against single bosses.

A practical rotation is to open with S3 for the crit setup, throw in a few normal attacks (or spam S3 to help break), then cast S2 right before the Ultimate to stack her damage buffs for the biggest possible finisher. Overall a low-maintenance, energy-free Green carry that wants to crit and stay healthy.
histoire: Élève de deuxième année au lycée préfectoral de jujutsu de Tokyo. Bien que née dans une famille d'exorcistes d'élite, elle n'a presque pas d'énergie occulte et ne peut même pas voir les fléaux sans lunettes. Dotée d'une condition physique exceptionnelle, elle vit en maniant des outils occultes.
