analyse: A Blue Hybrid attacker built around crits and Black Flash, who ramps his own damage through stacking self-buffs (Overtime Work) the longer the fight goes. He is a self-sufficient single-target carry that snowballs over time.
S2 is his self-buff button: it raises his Damage Dealt and amplifies any stat buffs he receives, making him hit progressively harder and synergize with external buffers.

S3 is his main damage skill — a hard-hitting multi-hit with a strong Crit Rate buff — and his Ultimate is a guaranteed-crit nuke that also strips the enemy's Crit Resistance, setting up even bigger crits afterward.

His engine is his passive suite: he starts with Cursed Energy and Ultimate gauge, regenerates energy every turn, and stacks Taijutsu & Jujutsu on every crit or Black Flash — plus a Black Flash triggers a massive Black Flash Rate boost, making his Black Flashes very consistent once rolling.

His SP upgrades transform him from a solo carry into a Blue-team buffer: with SP his S3 and passives hand the whole Blue team stacking Damage Dealt buffs (Overtime Work) on his crits and Black Flashes, so he amplifies the squad while dealing his own damage. Judge him largely on his SP form.
Overall a low-maintenance crit/Black-Flash carry who is good solo and excellent with SP unlocked — best in a Blue team that can feed him buffs to amplify and crit support to keep his engine spinning.
histoire: Un exorciste de grade 1 qui a démissionné de son poste d'employé de bureau. Un cadet de Gojo au lycée. Il avait compris que la carrière d'exorciste, c'était de la merde alors qu'il était encore lycéen, puis a découvert qu'être un employé ordinaire, c'était pareil après avoir travaillé dans une entreprise normale. Finalement, il a décidé de devenir exorciste, ce en quoi il excelle, et un adulte très mûr.

analyse: An SR Green debuffer who punches above his rarity thanks to a flexible toggle mechanic. He brings strong Damage Received debuffs and crowd control, making him a budget-friendly support option for Green teams that lack a debuffer.

His defining tool is the Alternate Tuning state, switched on and off with S2: it transforms his other skills between two modes — a straightforward debuff mode and a control mode — letting you adapt to what the fight needs.

S3 in normal mode applies a large, stackable Taijutsu & Jujutsu Damage Received debuff to all enemies (his main team-amplifying tool that builds up over multiple turns), and in Alternate Tuning it instead inflicts Stun and a chance of Confusion — flipping from amplification to lockdown.
His Ultimate is an AoE that lowers all enemies' Damage Dealt in normal mode, or in Alternate Tuning deals more damage and strips an Ultimate count from every enemy to delay their big moves.
S2 is cheap to cast and also buffs his own Jujutsu, so toggling Tuning costs almost nothing and keeps him flexible turn to turn.

As an SR he has low stats and no auto-skills, so he is not a long-term keeper for whales — but for newer players he is an accessible, genuinely useful Green debuffer and crowd-control unit until an SSR replacement is available.
histoire: Vieil homme d'âge indéterminé, directeur du lycée préfectoral de jujutsu de Kyoto. C'est aussi le principal chef de file des conservateurs dans le monde actuel des exorcistes. Il veut éliminer Itadori, qui a absorbé Sukuna.

analyse: A top-tier Yellow support who brings both buffs and debuffs in one package, making him a cornerstone of Yellow teams. Almost every action he takes either weakens the enemy or strengthens his allies.

S3 is his debuff workhorse: it has a high chance to Blind the target and stacks both a general Taijutsu & Jujutsu Damage Received debuff and a Yellow-type Damage Received debuff, softening enemies for the whole squad.
His Ultimate hits all enemies with a lasting Yellow-type Damage Received debuff while buffing the entire team's damage for several turns — a strong AoE setup-and-amplify button.

Both S2 and S1 stay useful: S2 lowers the enemy's Taijutsu Stat (reducing their Taijutsu damage) for a low Cursed Energy cost, and S1 (his normal attack) chips away enemy Crit Resistance at no cost at all.
His passive constantly buffs all allies' Taijutsu & Jujutsu Stat every turn, providing a steady stream of team damage with no input required.
A standout strength: his S2, S3 and Ultimate all ignore Blind, so unlike many characters he keeps functioning at full effectiveness even in content that spams Darkness.

analyse: A Green Hybrid attacker with a unique low-HP playstyle: she gets stronger the more hurt she is. Both her damage and her survivability scale up as her HP drops, so unlike most units she actively wants to be at low health rather than topped up.

Her standout mechanic is her characteristic: once her HP falls to 35% or below she gains an enormous Taijutsu & Jujutsu Stat boost every turn, turning her into a heavy hitter exactly when most units would be in danger.
Her S3 and Ultimate both scale their damage up as her HP gets lower, so they hit hardest in that same low-HP window — her S3 also charges a big chunk of Ultimate gauge to keep her nuke cycling.

S2 is her bread-and-butter strike that buffs her own Taijutsu, but it intentionally sacrifices some of her HP to cast — which is a feature, not a drawback, since it pushes her toward her powerful low-HP state faster.

She is built to survive at low health: a passive grants escalating damage reduction as her HP drops (huge at 35% or below), plus a one-time Revival with Attack Nullification, so she can sit safely in her danger zone. Her SP form adds a stacking damage buff based on attacks received and improves her sustain further.

She is a self-sufficient bruiser whose only real demand is getting low fast and staying there. Pair her with light healing at most — over-healing actually weakens her — and let her snowball in long single-target fights.

analyse: A Blue Hybrid Defender built around her Sword Sheath Count: a stacking resource that boosts her damage and, through a passive, grants her rotating defensive and offensive perks (damage reduction, break damage, then Crit Damage) as it climbs. Building and spending those stacks is the core of her gameplay.

Her SP upgrades transform her from a self-focused tank into a powerful Blue-team support — without SP she mostly protects and counters, but with SP unlocked her S3, counters and Ultimate all start handing big Taijutsu & Jujutsu buffs to the whole Blue team. Judge her on her SP form.

S2 is her defensive engine: it grants a Counter State, an evade chance, a taunt to pull enemies onto her, and a Sword Sheath stack — letting her bait melee attackers into her counters while building resource.
S3 buffs her own Taijutsu and adds Sword Sheath stacks; in its SP version it also buffs the entire Blue team's Taijutsu & Jujutsu, turning a personal buff into a team one.

Her Ultimate is a heavy hit that applies a Taijutsu Damage Received debuff and, at high Sword Sheath Count, cuts her own incoming damage. The SP Ultimate becomes an AoE, adds a Blue Damage Received debuff, buffs the whole team, and permanently upgrades her two auto-skills.

Her counter passive deals damage, charges her Ultimate and (in SP) buffs the Blue team's stats, so she generates value just by being attacked. She also synergizes with crit-based teammates since landing crits builds her Sword Sheath Count faster.
Overall a durable Blue Defender who, once her SP is online, doubles as one of the better Blue team buffers — best placed in a Blue squad that can feed her crits and let her soak hits.

analyse: A Red Taijutsu attacker who uses no Cursed Energy — all of his skills are free, so he never needs a battery and drops into any Red team. He is a self-sufficient, crit-focused bruiser whose specialty is cutting through enemy defenses.

His defining trait is defense-piercing: S2 ignores any Damage Reduction effects, while S3 and his Ultimate strip Attack Nullification and remove enemy buffs — making him a hard counter to bosses that hide behind shields, immunity or stacked buffs.
S2 is his main single-target nuke, hitting hard while bypassing the enemy's damage reduction. S3 adds break damage and is his tool for peeling away a buff and Attack Nullification on a single target.
His Ultimate is an AoE that strips Attack Nullification and a buff from every enemy before dealing heavy Taijutsu damage — a strong opener against buff-reliant enemy teams.

He is built around crits: his skills carry higher-than-normal Crit Damage, his normal attack lowers enemy Crit Resistance, and a passive stacks escalating Taijutsu buffs each time he crits — so he snowballs his own damage hard over the course of a fight.

His Physically Gifted passive makes him remarkably self-reliant — a large Taijutsu boost, HP regen, damage reduction, evasion, and immunity to some targeting effects. Overall a low-maintenance, energy-free Red carry that excels at punching through defensive bosses.

analyse: A Green Hybrid debuffer who relies on Cursed Energy to fuel his kit. His main job is amplifying the Green team's damage through debuffs, but with enough energy he hits hard enough to act as a secondary attacker too.

S2 and S3 are his debuff tools, each stacking a Green-type Damage Received debuff on the target — S2 increases Jujutsu Damage Received and S3 increases Taijutsu Damage Received, so you pick whichever matches your carry.
S1 deals combined damage that scales with his current Cursed Energy, rewarding him for keeping his pool topped up and giving him a free way to contribute damage between debuffs.
His Ultimate is a heavy combined-damage hit that also boosts his own break damage, restores Cursed Energy, and raises his maximum Cursed Energy cap — pushing his whole kit to a higher ceiling.

He keeps his own energy flowing through his characteristic (regenerating Cursed Energy every turn) and a passive that refunds energy on defeating enemies, so he stays self-sufficient without a dedicated battery.
Tip: since his Ultimate leans more on Jujutsu, pair it with S2 rather than S3 to set up the matching Jujutsu Damage Received debuff for maximum Ultimate damage.

analyse: A Yellow Jujutsu attacker who works as an AoE nuker with built-in survivability. His skills are extremely cheap (costing just 1 Cursed Energy), so he can cast freely and focus on charging his hard-hitting Ultimate.
His Ultimate is his main payoff: a powerful five-hit AoE Jujutsu nuke with escalating crit, making him excellent at clearing waves or pressuring an enemy team all at once.

S2 grants him Attack Immunity (with the trade-off of taking more damage while it lasts) and builds a stacking Jujutsu buff; once that buff is active the skill transforms into a self Damage and Crit Rate boost — so it doubles as both a defensive shield and a damage ramp. For maximum Ultimate damage you want to stack this S2 buff up to three times before firing it.
S3 is his single-target damage and control tool, hitting hard while lowering the enemy's damage output, giving him a way to soften a dangerous target between Ultimates.

He carries very high innate crit on his normal attack (which also self-taunts and charges his Ultimate faster) and a passive that stacks Damage Dealt on every crit, so he ramps his own damage steadily.

One thing to plan around: his Attack Immunity does not have perfect uptime — there is always one turn where it lapses and he is vulnerable, so be ready to protect him or play around that gap. Overall a self-sufficient Yellow AoE carry: he protects himself with Attack Immunity, costs almost no energy to operate, and snowballs crit-based damage toward his big AoE Ultimate. Best in a Yellow team that wants reliable wave clear and a durable attacker.

analyse: A Yellow Hybrid attacker who deals combined Taijutsu & Jujutsu damage and leans on Black Flash and a small debuff package. He is a straightforward single-target carry that also chips in some team utility through enemy debuffs.

His signature trick is Type Advantage: his S3 and Ultimate hit as if they had elemental advantage against the target without changing their type, so he deals bonus damage regardless of the enemy's element — making him a flexible pick that performs against any color of boss.
S3 is his key skill: it strikes with Type Advantage, lowers the enemy's Crit Resistance, and applies a Damage Received debuff — both a damage tool and a setup for the rest of the team.
His Ultimate is his payoff, a multi-hit that also lands with Type Advantage and guarantees a Black Flash on its final hit for a big spike of bonus damage.

He is self-sufficient on resources: a passive front-loads Cursed Energy and Ultimate gauge, regenerates energy each turn, buffs his own Jujutsu, and refunds more gauge whenever he hits with Type Advantage — and landing a Black Flash sharply raises his Black Flash rate.

His one demand is energy: S3 is fairly expensive to cast, so he benefits from a team that provides Cursed Energy support to keep firing it consistently. Overall a reliable, low-maintenance Yellow sub-DPS whose Type Advantage damage keeps him useful in almost any matchup, especially against enemies your main carry is weak into.
histoire: Un exorciste de grade 1 qui a démissionné de son poste d'employé de bureau. Un cadet de Gojo au lycée. Finalement, il a décidé de devenir exorciste, ce en quoi il excelle, et un adulte très mûr.

analyse: A Red Taijutsu Defender who tanks for the team while still hitting respectably — a sturdy front-liner that draws enemy fire, soaks it, and turns the punishment into damage. Much of his kit scales with his current Cursed Energy.

S2 is his core tank tool: it taunts the enemy onto himself and grants damage reduction that grows with his Cursed Energy, plus a Crit Resistance debuff on the target. Its SP form is a big upgrade, adding a team-wide taunt and damage reduction for all allies, making him a genuine team protector.

S3 (Kalpas Time) is his self-sustain and ramp: it heals him and buffs his Taijutsu based on his stacked Kalpas Count, scaling up to a large heal and damage boost — letting him stay alive in his tank role and hit hard when he cashes the stacks in.

His Ultimate is his payoff — a heavy multi-hit single-target nuke plus AoE and a self-heal — and a passive ramps its damage based on how many attacks he has taken, so the more he tanks, the harder his Ultimate lands.

He is very hard to kill: a Revival passive brings him back once per battle, his Kalpas mechanic and Ultimate keep healing him, and his damage reduction scales with energy — exactly what you want from a Defender.

Overall a durable Red tank-bruiser that protects the team and punishes incoming damage. He gets noticeably better with SP (team-wide protection and a stronger damage-taken passive), making him a strong defensive anchor for Red squads.

analyse: A Blue Taijutsu attacker built around relentless single-target pressure and Black Flash. He rewards focusing one enemy: a passive ramps his damage the more he attacks the same target, so he snowballs into a heavy hitter against bosses.
S2 is his bread-and-butter strike — strong damage with a Black Flash chance plus a Damage Received debuff on the target, softening the enemy for himself and the team.
S3 is his multi-hit damage skill and also charges Ultimate gauge for himself and the ally behind him, giving him a touch of support utility alongside his offense.
His Ultimate hits hard, has a chance to Stun, and grants him a long-lasting Crit Rate buff — both a burst and a setup that makes his follow-up attacks land more crits.

He doubles as a team protector through his passives: when an ally drops low he can taunt enemies onto himself, cut his damage taken, and he carries a self-Revival — useful sustain on top of his Poison/Soul resistance and a passive that lowers his skill costs after Black Flashes.

His SP form is a major upgrade that turns him into a Combo Count scaler — stacking large Taijutsu buffs as he attacks and takes hits, adding an enemy damage debuff, and improving his protective and energy tools. Judge his ceiling largely on his SP form, where he becomes a durable, ramping Blue single-target carry.
histoire: Élève de première année au lycée préfectoral de jujutsu de Tokyo. Un prodige qui n'apparaît qu'une fois par millénaire, capable de résister au poison virulent du roi des fléaux, Ryomen Sukuna. Il considère cette particularité comme une mission et se consacre personnellement à la lutte contre les fléaux.

analyse: A Green Jujutsu attacker who specializes in instant kills. Many of his skills can outright execute an enemy based on his Jujutsu Stat versus the target's remaining HP, making him a unique answer to high-HP adds and certain bosses that he can simply delete rather than chip down.

His Ultimate is the centerpiece — it deals percent-based HP damage to the whole enemy team and expands a Domain that, while active, makes every skill he uses carry a high-effectiveness instant kill and buffs his survivability. Crucially it grants him Guaranteed Hit and pierces enemy Attack Immunity, so it bypasses both defensive buffs on the enemy and accuracy debuffs on himself. It is his execution window where he is at his most dangerous.

S3 is his hardest-hitting skill and itself has an instant-kill chance; inside the Domain it gains a self Jujutsu buff and even stronger execute effectiveness, so it is his main damage and kill button.

S2 builds his Ultimate gauge and grants him evasion through Miniaturization; inside the Domain it transforms into a damaging attack with a Damage Received debuff and its own instant kill — turning a utility skill into another execution tool.

He also flexibly attacks using whatever element the target is weak to (regardless of his own type), so he ignores type disadvantages and stays effective against any color of enemy. A passive keeps him alive with HP regen and damage reduction that scale with low HP and high Cursed Energy.

His main drawback is the comedown after his Domain: it drains his Cursed Energy and blocks his Ultimate charge for a couple of turns. He is best used as a specialist executioner — bring him for content full of high-HP enemies he can instantly kill, where he massively outperforms a normal damage dealer.
histoire: Un fléau né des êtres humains. Il peut modifier l'apparence des humains en touchant leur âme. En tant que fléau tout juste né, il est fasciné par son pouvoir et répète sans cesse des expériences sur les humains avec innocence.

analyse: A Blue Taijutsu attacker who ramps his damage through Takada-chan's Guidance stacks. Most of his skills consume these stacks for big bonus damage, and his normal attack hits dramatically harder the more Guidance he has banked — so building and spending stacks is the core of his gameplay.

S2 is his stack generator and self-buff: it refreshes his Guidance count, boosts his Taijutsu, and grants damage reduction with a self-heal — making him both a damage-ramp tool and a survivability button in one.
S3 deals solid damage and reliably inflicts Confusion on the target; while Guidance is active it costs less, hits harder, and refunds some Cursed Energy — giving him control plus a damage spike.

His Ultimate is his payoff: a heavy single-target nuke that scales with his Guidance stacks, performs a guaranteed crit, heals him, and leaves behind a strong Taijutsu & Damage Dealt buff — so it both bursts and sets up his next few turns.

He is self-sufficient through his S2 heals and damage reduction, plus Black Flash access that boosts his crit. His SP form is a big upgrade: it adds a Revival, an evasion chance, and turns his Guidance stacks into escalating Taijutsu and Crit Damage buffs at the start of each turn — making him far stronger and tankier.

Overall a self-reliant Blue carry who snowballs through Guidance stacks. Manage your stacks to land empowered hits, and judge his ceiling largely on his SP form, which transforms him from a solid attacker into a durable, high-damage one.

analyse: A Yellow Taijutsu attacker specialized in Break damage. His whole kit pumps out break pressure and then capitalizes hard on enemies already in Break State, making him a top pick for break-focused content and bosses with break bars.

His standout strength is his Break payoff passive: he starts with bonus Break Damage and Damage Dealt, and once the target enters Break State his damage skyrockets — so the loop is break the enemy, then unload while they are vulnerable.

S3 and his Ultimate are his main damage, both adding large Break Damage boosts before hitting hard — the Ultimate is a heavy multi-hit single-target nuke, and his SP version pushes its numbers significantly higher.

S2 grants him a Counter and more break damage; its SP form is a major upgrade, adding self Taijutsu/crit buffs, a taunt, and a Damage Received debuff on whoever he counters — turning a defensive tool into team utility.

He is extremely sturdy as a puppet: a passive grants immunity to most status effects (Poison, Darkness, Stun, Confusion, Reverse Cursed Technique) and Instant Kill resistance, so he keeps functioning in content that disables other units.

Overall a durable, break-centric Yellow carry, best in teams or fights built around breaking enemies — and meaningfully stronger once his SP is unlocked. Note he cannot be paired with the Green Kokichi Muta version of the same character.

analyse: A Red Jujutsu attacker built around her Nail Count mechanic: she stacks Nails on enemies and then detonates them for a massive burst. The more Nails she has built up, the harder her payoff hits — so her gameplay is all about stacking and then cashing in.

"Hairpin" (S2) is her detonator and main damage: it hits every enemy carrying Nails and its damage scales enormously with how many Nails are stacked, reaching a huge multiplier at full stacks before clearing them. This is her burst window.

S1 and her normal attack are her cheap Nail-builders — S1 hits all enemies, stacks Nails, and applies a Jujutsu Damage Received debuff, while her normal attack stacks Nails on a single target and weakens its Jujutsu damage. You spend several turns building Nails before firing "Hairpin".

Her Ultimate is a hard-hitting Hybrid Damage strike that always lands a Black Flash and also adds a Nail, helping fuel her loop — and landing a Black Flash triggers a passive that grants a big, long-lasting Jujutsu buff and refunds Cursed Energy.

Her SP form sharpens the whole loop: it makes "Hairpin" cheaper and adds a Damage Received debuff, gives her Ultimate-charge support, and turns her Black Flash passive into an even bigger damage buff. Judge her ceiling largely on her SP form.

She is a strong burst-focused Red carry, but she needs setup turns and benefits from Cursed Energy support to fund her expensive detonation. Best used as a single-target/AoE nuker that stacks Nails patiently, then deletes a target — especially potent once her SP is unlocked.

analyse: A Blue Jujutsu attacker built around his Flowing Red Scale stance. Activating it buffs his damage, stats and Cursed Energy regen, and upgrades his other skills — so keeping the state up is the core of his gameplay.

S2 (Flowing Red Scale) is his engine: it turns on the state, granting a damage and Jujutsu boost plus passive energy regen. The catch is that when the state expires it leaves him with increased Damage Received, so you want to re-cast it before it lapses to stay safe and keep the buffs flowing.

S3 hits a single target normally, but while in Flowing Red Scale it converts into an AoE — and his normal attack also gains a big damage bonus and a self damage buff in the state, so his whole kit hits harder and wider once he is buffed up.
His Ultimate is his single-target nuke and gains an extra damage boost while in Flowing Red Scale, rewarding you for firing it during his buffed window.

His biggest strength, especially in his SP form, is team amplification through AoE debuffs: his SP S3 applies a strong Blue Damage Received debuff to all enemies at once, softening the entire field for the rest of the team while also dealing AoE damage. That turns him from a selfish self-buffer into a genuine Blue-team enabler.

His SP form also makes Flowing Red Scale far stronger overall — much bigger damage, stat and damage-reduction buffs that scale with his Cursed Energy, plus an Ultimate-charge boost and an auto-activation at the start of battle. Judge his ceiling largely on his SP form.

Overall a self-buffing Blue carry who, once SP is unlocked, doubles as an area debuffer that amplifies the whole team. Keep Flowing Red Scale active at all times and lean on his AoE Damage Received debuff in crit-focused Blue squads.
histoire: Élève de troisième année au lycée préfectoral de jujutsu de Kyoto. En toute circonstance, en tant que membre de l'une des trois grandes familles d'exorcistes, la famille Kamo, préserver la renommée de sa famille est le but de sa vie. Il pense de façon logique et agit avec détermination.

analyse: A Blue support whose entire job is amplifying the team's damage. She brings no real personal offense — her value is a stacked package of team-wide buffs and enemy debuffs that make a Blue carry hit far harder.
S2 is her flat damage buff: it raises all allies' Damage Dealt and Break Damage, a simple but powerful boost she keeps up to push the whole team's numbers.
S3 is her crit enabler: it grants the team Critical Hit Rate and Crit Damage while lowering all enemies' Crit Resistance — a triple boost that turns a crit-based carry into a consistent powerhouse.

Her normal attack quietly stacks a Damage Received debuff on the target, and her Ultimate is a strong AoE that has a high chance to Stun the enemy team and shaves an Ultimate count off the target — adding control and disruption on top of her buffs.

She is fragile with low stats, but a characteristic grants her evasion when her HP drops, giving her a bit of self-protection. Note she has no auto-skills, so all her value comes from actively casting her buffs.

Overall a pure Blue buffer-debuffer: slot her behind a Blue damage dealer, keep her two buff skills rolling, and use her Ultimate for control. She is best in crit-focused Blue teams that fully capitalize on the crit rate, crit damage and Crit Resistance shred she provides.

analyse: A Green Jujutsu debuffer-nuker on a timer: he is built to dish out heavy damage and debuffs over a limited window before leaving the field after 7 turns. Think of him as a burst specialist you bring out, unload, and rotate.

His Ultimate, Hollow Purple, is the payoff — a massive AoE Jujutsu nuke that also strips two Ultimate counts from every enemy to delay their big moves, then he exits the field. It is one of the hardest-hitting AoE buttons available and the whole point of fielding him.
S2 is his amplifier: it stacks a Damage Received debuff on the target and buffs his own damage, softening the enemy and ramping his own output for the team and his Ultimate.

S3 is his single-target damage and break tool, hitting hard while shaving the enemy's damage output. Both of his command skills cost almost nothing, so he can fire them freely every turn during his short stay.

He has extremely high innate crit and Black Flash on his normal attack (which also debuffs enemy damage), and a passive boosts his crit further on Black Flash — so he reliably crits for huge numbers in his window.

Crucially he starts with Attack Immunity, making him nearly untouchable while he operates. Overall a high-impact temporary carry: deploy him to debuff, crit hard, and detonate his AoE Ultimate, getting maximum value before his timer sends him off the field.

A meta caveat for the current game: his 7-turn limit (and the fact he leaves immediately after his Ultimate) has held him back over time, since modern stages tend to run much longer and reward units that can stay and sustain. His raw numbers are still excellent, but he is less reliable as a main carry now and works best in shorter fights or as a burst opener rather than a long-haul damage dealer.
histoire: Un enseignant capricieux et têtu du lycée préfectoral de jujutsu de Tokyo. Il adore jouer des tours aux autres et est reconnu par tous les exorcistes comme le plus puissant du monde. Il s'efforce maintenant de former la prochaine génération en alliés puissants afin que le monde des exorcistes ait un avenir plus radieux.

analyse: A straightforward Red Taijutsu attacker focused on single-target damage through crits and Black Flash. He has no complex gimmick — he simply buffs his own crit, ramps his Taijutsu, and hits hard, which makes him easy and reliable to pilot.

His Ultimate is his payoff: a heavy single-target nuke that always lands a Black Flash and leaves behind a Taijutsu Damage Received debuff on the target, both bursting the enemy and softening it for the team.

S3 is his main damage skill — it hits hard, stacks a Taijutsu self-buff, and charges a big chunk of Ultimate gauge, so it doubles as his damage button and his way to cycle his Ultimate quickly. At Limit Break 2 he can spam S3 to charge his Ultimate for several turns straight, sharpening his burst loop.
S2 is his crit setup: it sharply raises his own Critical Hit Rate and gives the whole team a stackable Break Damage buff, adding a touch of team support to his otherwise selfish kit.

His passives keep his crit and Black Flash engine spinning — landing a Black Flash boosts his Taijutsu and crits feed more crit rate, so he snowballs his own damage over the fight. He also resists Poison and Soul damage for a bit of innate durability.

Overall a clean, low-maintenance Red single-target carry. He wants crit and Cursed Energy support to keep his Ultimate and Black Flashes flowing, and he rewards focusing one target down rather than spreading damage.

analyse: A Yellow Jujutsu attacker who doubles as a powerful team amplifier through his Domain Expansion. He deals solid damage himself, but his real value is the Domain, which craters the enemy team's defenses and protects him at the same time.

His Ultimate, Chimera Shadow Garden, is the centerpiece: it hits hard with a guaranteed Stun and then expands a Domain that increases all enemies' Damage Received, lowers their Damage Dealt, grants him Attack Immunity, and makes his own skills cheaper — turning him into a near-untouchable amplifier for several turns.

While the Domain is active his other skills upgrade dramatically: S1 gains a massive Damage Received debuff on the target, S2 becomes a stronger AoE, and S3 turns into a heavy single-target hit with a big Damage Received debuff and a guaranteed Stun — so his whole kit comes online inside the Domain.
Outside the Domain he is a serviceable attacker with some baseline debuffs, but he is clearly built to fight from inside it; the Domain is where both his damage and his team utility peak.

He is also self-sufficient on resources: a characteristic refills his Ultimate gauge whenever his Cursed Energy runs low, helping him cycle his Domain, though the Domain drains his energy and blocks Ultimate charge once it ends.

The optimal setup is to open the Domain early, then stack his upgraded S1 on the target two or three times to pile its enormous Damage Received debuff before a teammate fires their own Ultimate into the softened enemy — making him a fantastic enabler for a burst carry. Note his Domain cannot overwrite an enemy Domain already in play, so cast it before other Domain users.

analyse: A Blue Jujutsu attacker who doubles as a damage amplifier, with a kit that scales almost everything off his own Cursed Energy. At full energy his damage and debuffs hit their ceiling, so keeping his pool high is the core of playing him.
He is self-fuelling: he naturally regenerates Cursed Energy every turn and recovers more whenever he defeats an enemy, so he rarely needs an external battery to stay near his cap.
S2 is his single-target debuff tool — it lowers the target's Taijutsu and stacks a Jujutsu Damage Received debuff, both scaling stronger the more energy he holds, softening a key target for the team.
S3 is his AoE: it damages all enemies and applies a team-wide Damage Received debuff, again scaling with his Cursed Energy, making him a strong opener that amplifies everyone's damage.
His Ultimate is a heavy AoE nuke whose damage ramps massively with his current Cursed Energy, but it drains a chunk of energy on use — so the rotation is about topping up to max, then unloading.

His SP form sharpens his AoE and Ultimate further and makes them scale on enemy count instead. Overall he is a flexible Blue debuffer-carry who rewards keeping his Cursed Energy bar as full as possible before committing his big skills.
histoire: Connu comme l'utilisateur de fléaux maléfique, il a un jour déclaré vouloir exterminer tous les non-exorcistes et créer un monde réservé aux exorcistes. Il a été banni du lycée de jujutsu pour avoir commis un massacre contre des humains ordinaires. C'est lui qui a ourdi la « Parade nocturne des cent démons ».

analyse: A versatile Red Jujutsu attacker who pairs heavy AoE damage with instant kills and a surprising amount of team support. He runs on an unusually large Cursed Energy pool, and much of his power scales with how much energy he is holding.

S2 (Cursed Speech) is his clear-and-debuff tool: AoE damage that scales with his Cursed Energy, a Jujutsu Damage Received debuff on the whole enemy team (also scaling with energy), and a chance to instantly kill weaker enemies based on his Jujutsu stat — excellent for wiping high-HP mobs.

S3 (Follow My Lead, Rika) is his single-target burst, a hard-hitting mixed-damage flurry with Black Flash chances; its SP version hits harder, buffs his own stats, ignores Darkness, and gets cheaper after his Ultimate.
His Ultimate is a massive AoE nuke that also buffs his own stats, making it one of his biggest damage windows, though it locks his Ultimate gauge for a few turns afterward.

Beyond damage he doubles as a sustain unit: a passive heals the whole team when allies drop low (while charging his own Ultimate), he counters melee attackers, and his Black Flash and crit passives keep ramping his Jujutsu.

His SP form sharpens everything — stronger S3, better Black Flash scaling, more team healing, and bigger counters — turning him into a high-value all-rounder. Judge his ceiling largely on his SP form, where he becomes a flexible Red carry that nukes, executes, and keeps the team alive at once. He simply wants Cursed Energy uptime to stay at full power.
histoire: Un lycéen de dernière année qui voulait autrefois mourir à cause de Rika, sa petite amie transformée en fléau. Depuis son inscription au lycée de jujutsu, sa vie est devenue plus positive grâce à la camaraderie qu'il y a trouvée. Il a décidé de lever la malédiction de Rika.

analyse: A Yellow Jujutsu Obstructor who blends Poison damage-over-time with debuffs and a protective tanking role. His standout theme is that many of his debuffs scale stronger the more turns of Poison the enemy is carrying — so the longer his Poison stays ticking, the harder he weakens the target.

S3 (Poison Stab) is his core tool: it deals damage, applies long-lasting Poison, and stacks a large Damage Received debuff on the target that grows with the Poison already present — making it both his main debuff and the setup for the rest of his kit.

His Ultimate hits hard, refreshes Poison, and lowers the enemy's Jujutsu Stat (again scaling with Poison duration), so it caps off his debuff stack while dealing his biggest single hit. His Poison is also a relatively rare status that few units can apply, giving him niche value.

S1 is a strong tool against Jujutsu-type enemies: it stacks a Jujutsu Stat reduction on the target, sharply cutting their Jujutsu damage output — making him a soft counter to Jujutsu attackers. Note that every one of his skills, even S1, costs Cursed Energy.

S2 (Moon Dregs) is his protective tool: he taunts all enemies onto himself, grants himself Attack Nullification, buffs his own Jujutsu, and cuts the team's damage taken — letting him soak a turn of enemy fire to shield the squad.

A passive ramps his damage based on how many Tokyo Jujutsu High allies are on the team, rewarding themed Yellow line-ups. His SP form is a big upgrade: it turns S2 into a much stronger team-protection button (more damage reduction, team stat buffs, Stun immunity for an ally) and strengthens his Poison and debuffs.

Overall a debuff-and-protect Obstructor rather than a pure damage dealer. He is at his best in Poison/DoT-focused Yellow teams where his scaling debuffs amplify the squad — and noticeably stronger once his SP is unlocked.

analyse: A Blue Jujutsu attacker who blends break-focused damage, control, and debuffs through his Divine Dog (Totality) shikigami. He is at his best against enemies in Break State, where his damage spikes hard.

His Ultimate summons Divine Dog: Totality while dealing heavy damage. Once the dog is out, his other skills and normal attack all gain bonus Jujutsu hits and ignore Darkness, so keeping the dog active is the core of his gameplay. The dog also tanks for him, reducing the damage he takes.

S2 (Nue) is his control and debuff tool: it deals damage with a near-guaranteed Stun and stacks a Blue Jujutsu Damage Received debuff on the target, both locking down a threat and softening it for the team.
S3 (Max Elephant) is his AoE clear, hitting all enemies for solid Jujutsu damage — useful for waves between his single-target work.

His real strength is break synergy: his skills and Ultimate pile on break damage, and a passive massively boosts his damage against enemies already in Break State, so he excels in break-focused teams that can crack the enemy open for him.

His SP form is a major upgrade — the SP Ultimate gives the Divine Dog real HP so it tanks a share of incoming damage, hits much harder, and his SP passive adds Ultimate-charge and a damage buff on kills. Judge his ceiling largely on his SP form, where he becomes a durable break-carry and disruptor.

analyse: A Blue Jujutsu attacker built around Flame damage-over-time and his Domain Expansion. He layers burning DoT on enemies that scales with his Cursed Energy, then capitalizes inside his Domain where his whole offense spikes.

His Ultimate, Coffin of the Iron Mountain, is the centerpiece: it deals AoE damage and expands a Domain that blankets all enemies in heavy Flame DoT while granting him a massive Crit Rate boost, more Damage Dealt, damage reduction, Guaranteed Hit, Attack Immunity Nullification, and Cursed Energy back. It is his power window where he goes from solid to dominant.

S2 (Hellfire) is his single-target damage and DoT applier with a Guaranteed Hit, and his normal attack also applies Flame DoT — both scaling stronger the more Cursed Energy he holds, so keeping his energy high deepens his burn damage.
S3 (Ember Insects) is a random-target multi-hit, useful for spreading damage across a group between his stronger buttons.
He is fairly self-sufficient: passives refund Cursed Energy when he runs low and surge his Jujutsu when his HP drops, giving him a comeback spike in dangerous moments.

His SP form is a major upgrade — a stronger, longer Domain that refunds even more energy, plus an SP passive that adds evasion and a Cursed-Energy-scaling damage buff, and empowers his Ghost Lights. Judge his ceiling largely on his SP form, where he becomes a high-output Flame Domain carry. Keep his Cursed Energy high to maximize his burn and stay inside his Domain to unleash his full damage.

analyse: An SR Healer whose value is pure sustain. She is a budget-friendly dedicated healer that keeps the team alive, useful for newer or free-to-play players who lack a stronger support.
S3 (Reverse Cursed Technique) is her single-target heal — a strong, cheap restore she can use freely to top up whichever ally needs it most.

Her Ultimate is her team heal, restoring HP to all allies at once — her biggest safety button for recovering the whole squad after heavy damage. Be aware its gauge is slow to charge, so save it for when the team genuinely needs a big recovery.
S2 (Sample Retrieval) adds a little offensive utility: it deals minor damage and chips away at the enemy's Crit Resistance, giving crit-based carries a small boost between heals.

Her healing scales off her Jujutsu stat — and since it has no element restriction, she can heal allies of any color, fitting into any team that needs reliable sustain. Because it scales with Jujutsu, buffing her Jujutsu stat (via allies or memories) directly increases how much she heals. One quirk: her heals do not work on Cursed Spirit allies — they take slight damage instead.

As an SR she has very low stats and no auto-skills, so she is a stopgap rather than an end-game keeper. Bring her early on to survive content while you build toward an SSR healer, then retire her once you have a stronger option.

analyse: One of the game's original launch units: a Blue Jujutsu attacker with a deliberately simple, high-impact kit. He hits extremely hard with very high crit damage and almost no setup, but he is a temporary unit who leaves the field after 7 turns.

His Ultimate is a powerful AoE Jujutsu nuke, and his S2 is a hard-hitting single-target strike with a high Black Flash chance — both of his command skills cost just 1 Cursed Energy, so he can fire them freely every turn without needing energy support.

S3 is his self-buff, a large flat Damage boost he casts early to amplify everything he does for the next few turns. Combined with his high innate crit damage, it lets him put up huge numbers in a short window.

He starts with Attack Immunity, making him nearly untouchable while active, and a passive boosts his crit on Black Flash. There is essentially no complexity to him — buff with S3, then unload his skills and Ultimate before his timer runs out.

A meta caveat for the current game: as an early unit, his 7-turn limit has aged poorly. Modern stages tend to run much longer and reward units that can stay and sustain, so he now works best in shorter fights or as a free, accessible burst opener rather than a long-term carry. His raw damage is still respectable, but he has been outpaced by newer, longer-lasting attackers.
Overall a beginner-friendly, no-strings Blue nuker — great value early on for free-to-play players, but more of a situational burst piece than a main carry in today's meta.

analyse: A Green Taijutsu attacker built entirely around Black Flash. His whole kit exists to land Black Flashes as often as possible and snowball off them, making him a dedicated single-target Black Flash carry.

S2 (Attentive) is his setup button: it grants enormous Critical Hit Rate and Black Flash Rate buffs plus a chunk of Ultimate gauge — you cast it first to massively boost his chance of landing Black Flashes before he starts swinging.

S3 is his main damage skill, a multi-hit that strips the enemy's Crit Resistance and has multiple Black Flash chances per cast. Its SP version hits much harder, deepens the Crit Resistance shred, and massively amplifies its Black Flash damage.
His Ultimate is a guaranteed Black Flash on its first hit with boosted Black Flash and Crit Damage across the strike — his single biggest payoff, and the centerpiece of his burst.

His engine is his Zone passive: landing a Black Flash sends him into Zone for big Black Flash rate and Taijutsu buffs plus Cursed Energy, which makes his next Black Flashes even more likely — a self-reinforcing loop. The SP version of this passive is a huge upgrade, roughly doubling his Taijutsu and adding bonus Black Flash damage.

He also resists Poison and Soul damage for some durability. Overall a Black-Flash-focused Green carry that snowballs hard once rolling — and noticeably stronger with SP unlocked, where his Zone state turns him into a powerhouse. Best paired with Cursed Energy support to keep his loop firing.

analyse: A Green Taijutsu Tank with a two-phase identity: he starts as a defensive front-liner that protects the team, then transforms into an offensive bruiser once he enters Gorilla Mode through his Ultimate.

In his base form his job is protection — S2 taunts all enemies onto himself and grants heavy damage reduction, soaking a turn of enemy fire to shield the squad while he charges toward his transformation.

His Ultimate flips him into Gorilla Mode: it deals damage, ignores counters, and grants a big Taijutsu boost, but locks him out of using his Ultimate afterward. In exchange, his skills all upgrade into aggressive versions.

Once in Gorilla Mode his kit becomes offensive: his normal attack and S3 gain bonus break damage and AoE, and his former taunt skill (S2) instead pumps a large Taijutsu buff into himself — turning the protective tank into a heavy hitter.

He is very durable throughout: a Revival lets him survive a lethal blow once per battle, he has innate damage reduction in base form, and a passive grants him a big stat and damage surge when his Ultimate gauge is full in Gorilla Mode.

Overall a tank-into-bruiser that opens by protecting the team, then transforms into a sturdy Green damage dealer. Best used where you want a front-liner who can absorb early pressure and then take over as a secondary attacker once Gorilla Mode is online.

analyse: A Green Hybrid attacker built around crits and Black Flash. He deals combined Taijutsu & Jujutsu damage and ramps his own output through crit-driven self-buffs, making him a reliable damage dealer that can both single-target and clear waves.

S2 (Cursed Technique Disclosure) is his setup button: it grants a large Critical Hit Rate and Break Damage buff for several turns, which you cast first to make his crits land consistently before he starts attacking.
S3 (Ratio Technique) is his single-target burst, a hard-hitting multi-hit with high Crit Damage and Black Flash chances — his main button against priority targets.

His Ultimate is an 8-hit AoE that scales up further with every crit it lands, so the more crit he has stacked the harder it hits across the whole enemy team. Its SP version is a major upgrade, adding a chance to Stop enemy actions and a team-wide Green Damage Received debuff — turning his nuke into a team amplifier.

His passives keep the crit engine spinning: crits and Black Flashes grant big Taijutsu & Jujutsu buffs, a Black Flash sharply raises his Black Flash rate, and a later-turn passive refills his energy and Ultimate gauge — so he snowballs the longer the fight goes.

Overall a clean crit/Black-Flash Green carry that gets a meaningful upgrade with SP, where his Ultimate becomes an AoE nuke plus debuff. Judge his ceiling largely on his SP form, and pair him with crit support to keep his self-buffs and Ultimate scaling.

analyse: An SR Red support who punches above his rarity as a simple but effective buffer-debuffer. With no flashy gimmick, he just buffs the team and weakens enemies — a budget-friendly support for Red teams that lack a dedicated one.

S2 (Tutoring) is his core buff: a clean Taijutsu & Jujutsu Stat boost to the whole team that lasts several turns, the main reason to bring him. Crucially, his buffs and debuffs have no element restriction — they work for allies of any color, so unlike many supports who only boost their own element he can slot into any team regardless of composition.
S3 (Let's Go, Cathy!) is his debuff tool — it deals multi-hit damage and stacks a Damage Received increase on the target, softening a key enemy for the team's carry.
His Ultimate caps off his support package: heavy single-target damage plus both a stat reduction and a Damage Received debuff on the enemy, so it both hurts and amplifies the team's follow-up.

As an SR his stats are low and he has no auto-skills, so he is a stopgap rather than an end-game keeper — but for newer or free-to-play players he is an accessible, genuinely useful Red support until an SSR replacement comes along.

analyse: A Red Taijutsu attacker who doubles as a support through his Best Friend mechanic. He partners with a chosen ally, buffing them and himself while protecting that ally with a counter — so he is as much a force-multiplier for a carry as he is a damage dealer.

S2 (Blast From The Past) is his signature: it buffs his own and a chosen ally's Taijutsu and tags that ally as Best Friend. When the Best Friend is attacked, Todo counters for damage and inflicts Disruption — giving him a defensive bodyguard role on top of his buffs.

S3 (Boogie Woogie) is his single-target damage and control tool, dealing damage with a chance to apply Disruption to the target. Note it always acts at the lowest action priority, so it resolves at the end of the turn.

His Ultimate is a hard-hitting multi-hit that grants a Critical Hit Rate buff to himself and also to his Best Friend ally, doubling down on his amplifier role and turning him and his partner into a crit-heavy duo.
He runs on crits and Black Flash: a passive sends him into Zone for bonus crit after a Black Flash, and defeating enemies stacks his Taijutsu — so he ramps his own offense over a fight.

His own damage is relatively low for an attacker, so lean into his support role rather than expecting him to carry. A couple of practical notes: his Best Friend always goes to the ally positioned behind him (wrapping around, so a 4th-slot Todo buffs the 1st-slot ally), and his counter costs Cursed Energy to fire — pair him with a battery or CE memory to keep it active.

Overall a hybrid attacker-support best paired with a strong carry he can designate as Best Friend. Slot a damage dealer behind him so Todo can buff them, crit alongside them, and counter anyone who attacks them — he is at his best enabling a partner rather than fighting solo.

analyse: An R-rarity Red support who punches above his rarity through team protection and control. Despite being the lowest tier of unit, his kit does genuinely useful things, making him a handy early-game pick for free-to-play players.

S2 (Protect!) is his standout tool: it cuts the whole team's Damage Received and fills every ally's Ultimate gauge — a rare combination of defensive shielding and Ultimate acceleration that even some higher-rarity units lack.
S3 (Don't Move!) is his control button, a near-guaranteed single-target Stun that can lock down a dangerous enemy for a turn.
His Ultimate is a solid single-target Cursed Speech nuke, giving him a bit of damage to contribute alongside his support.
The cost of his kit is his own HP — nearly everything he does sacrifices health to cast — and as an R he is extremely fragile with very low stats.

In practice his main current use is as a one-shot Ultimate enabler: you cast S2 to instantly fill the whole team's Ultimate gauge, letting your carries unleash their Ultimates early, and accept that he bleeds himself out doing it. He is essentially expendable — a cheap battery you sacrifice to kickstart the team's burst, then replace with a real SSR support.

analyse: A Red Taijutsu attacker who uses no Cursed Energy at all — every skill is free, so she never needs a battery and drops into any Red team. Her damage is pure Taijutsu and she leans on her passives to ramp her stats over the fight.

Her standout trait is that she gets stronger the more enemies are present: a passive scales her Taijutsu sharply with enemy count, making her especially strong in waves and crowded fights rather than single-target duels.

S3 is her AoE clear — a hit-all strike on a short cooldown — and S2 is her single-target damage that also lowers the enemy's Taijutsu output, so between them she handles both packs and priority targets.

Her Ultimate is a hard-hitting two-hit nuke, and its SP version is a major upgrade that scales its damage with her current HP (peaking when she is healthy), rewarding you for keeping her topped up. Her SP normal attack also adds Ultimate charge and a self Taijutsu buff, smoothing her ramp.
She is self-sufficient and durable thanks to her Heavenly Restriction passive — passive HP regen, damage reduction, and the enemy-count Taijutsu scaling — plus a wave-start crit and stat boost.

Overall a low-maintenance, energy-free Red carry who shines against multiple enemies and gets a significant power bump from her SP form. Judge her ceiling largely on her SP, and keep her HP high to maximize her Ultimate.

analyse: A Red Jujutsu debuffer-attacker built around enemy damage reduction and self-sustain. He weakens the enemy team's offense while soaking pressure himself, making him a durable disruptor more than a pure carry.

His Ultimate, Shining Sea of Growing Branches, expands a Domain that lowers all enemies' Damage Dealt and grants him Guaranteed Hit plus Attack Immunity Nullification — so it both protects the team by softening enemy damage and guarantees his attacks land, even punching through defensive bosses. It can also overwrite an enemy Domain already in play. The catch is that his Ultimate is slow to charge, and it cannot build at all while his own Domain is active.
S3 (Terra Pulchra) is his main team-protection tool: it cuts all enemies' Damage Dealt and sharply boosts his own Ultimate charge, letting him cycle his Domain faster while shielding the squad.
S2 (Roots Piercing) is his single-target damage, and his normal attack deals more the higher the enemy's Ultimate count, giving him a niche damage bump against units building toward their Ultimate.

He is very self-sufficient: passives regenerate his HP each turn, refund Cursed Energy when he runs low, and grant innate damage reduction — so he stays alive and operating without needing external support.

Two weaknesses to plan around: he is hard-countered by Flame damage (avoid him against fire-heavy content), and he cannot be healed by Reverse Cursed Technique — in fact RCT damages him — so he relies entirely on his own regen for sustain. Overall a sturdy Red debuffer who shines by neutering the enemy team's damage and outlasting them, best used as a defensive disruptor rather than a front-line damage dealer.

analyse: A pure support whose value comes entirely from his utility, not his stats. Despite being only an R rarity, he is one of the most widely used battery units in the game because his kit does exactly what most teams need.
S3 is the reason he sees so much play: it feeds Cursed Energy to the whole team every turn, keeping expensive carries firing their skills and Ultimates far more often than they could on their own.
S2 is a single-target damage reduction shield he can drop on whichever ally is under threat, giving him a bit of defensive flexibility on top of his energy support.
His Ultimate hands the whole team a large Jujutsu Stat buff, making him a genuine damage amplifier for Jujutsu-focused comps rather than just an energy stick.

He brings no real personal damage and is fragile, so he sits in the back doing his job. Slot him in any team that struggles to keep Cursed Energy flowing — he is a cheap, accessible solution to the most common bottleneck in team building.

analyse: A Yellow Jujutsu attacker who blends Nail Count stacking with Soul damage and aggressive self-buffs. She builds Nails on enemies and detonates them with her Ultimate, and several of her hits attack the Soul directly, letting her bypass certain defenses.

Her Ultimate is her payoff: it scales massively with how many Nails are stacked on the target (huge at full stacks), hits everything carrying Nails, then clears them. Building Nails first and then firing it is her core damage loop. Its SP version adds even more damage scaling and a team-wide Jujutsu Damage Received debuff.

S3 (Resonance) is a high-damage Soul strike whose damage rises the lower her own HP is — rewarding aggressive, risky play — and its SP version hits harder, gains a Stop chance, shreds Crit Resistance, and ignores Darkness, making it a strong single-target nuke.
S2 (I'll destroy you) is her self-buff, a flat Jujutsu Damage boost she casts to ramp her output, and her normal attack stacks Nails on a single target to set up her Ultimate.
A characteristic rewards focusing one enemy — repeatedly attacking the same target increases her Damage Dealt — so she snowballs against bosses and priority targets she can lock onto.

Overall a burst-focused Yellow carry built around stacking Nails and detonating them, with extra reach through Soul damage. She gets a clear power bump from her SP form (bigger Ultimate, stronger S3, plus a team debuff), so judge her ceiling largely on her SP.

analyse: A Yellow Jujutsu support whose standout role is keeping the team alive. His signature passive lets him outright nullify fatal attacks that would defeat an ally — a powerful safety net that can save runs against hard-hitting bosses, usable a few times per battle.

The cost of his kit is his own HP: most of his actions, and especially that life-saving nullify, sacrifice his health to work (more against powerful enemies). He offsets this with self-heals, but managing his HP is the core of playing him.

S2 (Smash It) is his offensive contribution: it deals damage and stacks a Damage Received debuff on the target while boosting his own break damage, so he chips in some team amplification between his protective duties.
S3 (Throat Medicine) is his self-sustain — a Cursed-Energy-free heal he uses to recover the HP his kit constantly bleeds, on a cooldown so it cannot be spammed endlessly.

His Ultimate is his biggest single hit, dealing heavy Jujutsu damage that scales up when his own HP is high — and notably high for a support unit, so he is not purely passive on offense. This creates a tension where he wants to stay healthy for damage but is constantly sacrificing HP to protect the team.

Overall a defensive Yellow support built around a unique death-prevention tool. He is not a damage carry; bring him to survive brutal content, lean on his heals to manage his HP cost, and value him for turning otherwise lethal hits into non-events.
